requirements.text: record.Recorder.WriteTo followed by record.ReadFrom shall reproduce every entry's Requester, Request, and Response fields unchanged.

requirements.title: ReadFrom detects a corrupted log with ErrCorrupted
requirements.text: record.ReadFrom shall return an error wrapping ErrCorrupted when a logged entry's payload does not match its trailing CRC32.

requirements.title: Replay feeds recorded requests into a target Handler in order
requirements.text: record.Replay shall call target.HandleRequest once per recorded request, in the same order as Snapshot, and shall return the responses received.

requirements.title: Handler HandleRequest is safe for concurrent use
requirements.text: record.Handler.HandleRequest shall be safe for concurrent calls without data races.

requirements.title: Controller StreamID delegates to the inner Controller
requirements.text: observe's wrapped Controller StreamID method shall return exactly the inner Controller's own StreamID.

requirements.title: Controller Request delegates to the inner Controller and returns its response
requirements.text: observe's wrapped Controller Request method shall call the inner Controller's Request with the given addr/control/body and return its response unchanged on success.

requirements.title: A successful Request records latency and sets health true for a non-error response
requirements.text: observe's wrapped Controller Request method shall, on success, call Metrics.ObserveRequestLatency once and call Metrics.SetEndpointHealth with healthy=true when the response carries no acf.FlagError.

requirements.title: A successful Request with a FlagError response sets health false
requirements.text: observe's wrapped Controller Request method shall call Metrics.SetEndpointHealth with healthy=false when a successful Request's response carries acf.FlagError.

requirements.title: A failing Request increments the error counter without recording latency or health
requirements.text: observe's wrapped Controller Request method shall, when the inner Controller.Request errors, call Metrics.IncRequestError and shall not call ObserveRequestLatency or SetEndpointHealth.

requirements.title: A timeout-shaped error also increments the deadline-miss counter
requirements.text: observe's wrapped Controller Request method shall call Metrics.IncDeadlineMiss when the inner Controller.Request's error wraps udp.ErrTimeout or context.DeadlineExceeded.

requirements.title: Controller Close is idempotent and closes the inner Controller
requirements.text: observe's wrapped Controller Close method shall be safe to call more than once and shall call Close on the inner Controller.

requirements.title: Controller Request is safe for concurrent use
requirements.text: observe's wrapped Controller Request method shall be safe for concurrent calls without data races.

requirements.title: Handler with no rules delegates directly to the wrapped Handler
requirements.text: faultinject.Handler.HandleRequest shall delegate directly to the wrapped request.Handler when no Rule is currently active.

requirements.title: FaultDrop returns an error without reaching the wrapped Handler
requirements.text: faultinject.Handler.HandleRequest, with an active FaultDrop rule, shall return a non-nil error and must not call the wrapped request.Handler.

requirements.title: FaultSlow sleeps at least Latency then forwards to the wrapped Handler
requirements.text: faultinject.Handler.HandleRequest, with an active FaultSlow rule, shall sleep at least Rule.Latency, then call the wrapped request.Handler.

requirements.title: FaultCRCFailure returns e2e.ErrCRCMismatch without reaching the wrapped Handler
requirements.text: faultinject.Handler.HandleRequest, with an active FaultCRCFailure rule, shall return an error wrapping e2e.ErrCRCMismatch and must not call the wrapped request.Handler.

requirements.title: FaultSafeStateEntry returns request.ErrPurgedByWatchdog
requirements.text: faultinject.Handler.HandleRequest, with an active FaultSafeStateEntry rule, shall return an error wrapping request.ErrPurgedByWatchdog.

requirements.title: FaultDiscoveryClaimTimeout returns discovery.ErrNotConfigurationClaimant
requirements.text: faultinject.Handler.HandleRequest, with an active FaultDiscoveryClaimTimeout rule, shall return an error wrapping discovery.ErrNotConfigurationClaimant.

requirements.title: FaultCancellation returns request.ErrTicketCancelled
requirements.text: faultinject.Handler.HandleRequest, with an active FaultCancellation rule, shall return an error wrapping request.ErrTicketCancelled.

requirements.title: A Count-based rule fires exactly Count times then auto-expires
requirements.text: faultinject.Handler, given a Rule with Count>0, shall apply that rule on exactly the next Count matching calls, then fall through to the wrapped Handler on subsequent calls; ClearRules shall remove every active rule immediately.

requirements.title: Handler HandleRequest and AddRule are safe for concurrent use
requirements.text: faultinject.Handler.HandleRequest and AddRule shall be safe for concurrent calls without data races.

requirements.title: Update rejects an empty image
requirements.text: firmware.Updater.Update shall return ErrImageEmpty for a zero-length image.

requirements.title: Update rejects an image larger than MaxImageSize
requirements.text: firmware.Updater.Update shall return ErrImageTooLarge for an image longer than MaxImageSize.

requirements.title: Update delivers chunks with consistent CRC32 and advancing offsets
requirements.text: firmware.Updater.Update shall deliver every chunk via its configured TransportFunc carrying the whole image's CRC-32 in every chunk's ChunkPayload.CRC32, with ChunkPayload.Offset advancing by ChunkSize per chunk.

requirements.title: A FlagError chunk response aborts delivery with ErrEndpointRejected
requirements.text: firmware.Updater.Update shall stop sending further chunks and return an error wrapping ErrEndpointRejected as soon as a chunk delivery's response carries acf.FlagError.

requirements.title: A FlagError verify response reports ErrCRCMismatch
requirements.text: firmware.Updater.Update shall return ErrCRCMismatch when the post-install verify call's response carries acf.FlagError.

requirements.title: A fully-acknowledged Update reports no error
requirements.text: firmware.Updater.Update shall return nil when every chunk delivery and the verify call succeed without acf.FlagError.

requirements.title: Concurrent Update calls on one Updater are serialized with ErrUpdateInProgress
requirements.text: firmware.Updater.Update shall return ErrUpdateInProgress immediately for a call that arrives while another Update on the same Updater is still in progress.

requirements.title: ChunkPayload Marshal/UnmarshalChunkPayload round-trips every field
requirements.text: firmware.UnmarshalChunkPayload applied to firmware.ChunkPayload.Marshal's output shall reproduce TotalSize, Offset, CRC32, and Data unchanged.

requirements.title: evt[3] and evt[2:0] are read as the two independent fields TC18 §13.5 defines
requirements.text: acf.Message.EVTSelector shall return the request's evt[2:0] value with the evt[3] request-acknowledge bit masked off, and acf.Message.EVTAckRequested shall report evt[3]. acf.ClassifyEVT shall produce the same result for a given evt[2:0] whether or not evt[3] is set.

requirements.title: ClassifyEVT implements Table 30's SPI row
requirements.text: acf.ClassifyEVT for acf.EVTClassChannelSelect shall map evt[2:0] = 000b..101b to EVTActionInterface on channels 0..5 respectively, return acf.ErrEVTReserved for 110b, and map 111b to EVTActionConfigure, per TC18 §13.5 Table 30's SPI row. It shall return acf.ErrEVTUnknownClass for a class value outside Table 30's three rows.

requirements.title: ClassifyEVT implements Table 30's ADC/PWM_IN/I2C/LIN/CAN/UART/ISELED/MDIO row
requirements.text: acf.ClassifyEVT for acf.EVTClassConfigOnly shall map evt[2:0] = 000b to EVTActionInterface, return acf.ErrEVTReserved for 001b through 110b, and map 111b to EVTActionConfigure. The 000b mapping is a documented departure from TC18 §13.5 Table 30's literal "000b to 110b reserved" text, adopted because §13.7.9 Figure 33 shows a conformant request with evt = 0000b and §13.7.7.3 requires an ordinary payload to reach the interface; the departure shall remain documented at acf.ClassifyEVT.

requirements.title: ClassifyEVT implements Table 30's GPIO/PWM_OUT row
requirements.text: acf.ClassifyEVT for acf.EVTClassArithmetic shall map evt[2:0] = 000b/001b/010b/011b/101b/110b to the set/OR/AND/XOR/saturating-add/saturating-subtract combining rules respectively, return acf.ErrEVTReserved for 100b, and map 111b to EVTActionConfigure, per TC18 §13.5 Table 30's GPIO/PWM_OUT row.

requirements.title: CheckEVTPayloadPresence implements TC18 §12.9.1's general payload rule
requirements.text: acf.CheckEVTPayloadPresence shall return acf.ErrEVTMissingPayload when evt[2:0] is non-zero and the request carries no byte_msg_payload, and nil otherwise, per TC18 §12.9.1: "If evt[2:0] ≠ 0 and no byte_msg_payload is present, then an error response shall be sent with the error code = UNSUPPORTED_CMD". acf.Message.EVTDisposition shall apply this rule before Table 30's per-type interpretation.

requirements.title: ApplyEVTWriteOp implements Table 30's combining rules and saturation
requirements.text: acf.ApplyEVTWriteOp shall compute payload, payload|current, payload&current, payload^current, a saturating payload+current and a saturating payload-current for the six combining rules of TC18 §13.5 Table 30's GPIO/PWM_OUT row; the arithmetic rules shall saturate at zero on the low side and at the caller-supplied bound on the high side rather than wrapping; and the subtraction shall use the operand order the table states normatively (byte_msg_payload minus current interface status).

requirements.title: Configuration-request body codec round-trips TC18 §12.7.1 Figure 18
requirements.text: acf.EncodeConfigRequestBody/DecodeConfigRequestBody shall round-trip a configuration request's byte_msg_payload as a big-endian 16-bit relative EP_func register start address followed by the configuration data, and DecodeConfigRequestBody shall return acf.ErrShortConfigRequest rather than panicking for a body too short to hold that address.

requirements.title: Endpoint dispatch is keyed on the (stream_id, byte_bus_id) pair
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — udp.Router shall resolve a request's endpoint from a configurable look-up table keyed on the pair (avtp.Header.StreamID, acf.Message.ByteBusID), so two RC Clients may address the same endpoint under different byte_bus_id values and the same byte_bus_id on two streams may resolve to two different endpoints. Today Router.handlers is keyed on ByteBusID alone. TC18 §10.1 (TC18.txt:1020-1022), restated at §12.9.1 (TC18.txt:3194-3196) and §13.1 (TC18.txt:3501).

requirements.title: Every response echoes the request's byte_bus_id and transaction_num
requirements.text: Every response an endpoint or udp.errorResponse emits shall carry the originating request's ByteBusID and TransactionNum unchanged, since a response's stream target is derived from the byte_bus_id the request carried rather than from any server-side address. TC18 §10.1 (TC18.txt:1023-1024), §11.3 Table 15 (TC18.txt:1881-1885), §12.9.1 (TC18.txt:3213) and §12.9.6 (TC18.txt:3410-3411).

requirements.title: The destination (multicast) address is derived from the stream identification
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The l2 and udp send paths shall derive each frame's destination (multicast) address from the avtp.StreamID carried inside the AVTPDU rather than accepting a caller-supplied destination that may contradict it. l2.EncodeFrame and l2.Transport.Send take dst as a parameter today. TC18 §10.2 (TC18.txt:1032-1033).

requirements.title: Requests carrying an unknown stream_id are discarded
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The receive path shall discard, without invoking any request.Handler and without replying, a request whose avtp.Header.StreamID is not among the streams the addressed endpoint is configured to listen to. TC18 §13.1 (TC18.txt:3500-3501) and §12.8.2 (TC18.txt:3171-3173).

requirements.title: A TSCF-headed request executes no earlier than its presentation time
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — udp.Router.Route shall defer a request whose avtp.Header.Disposition reports DispositionScheduled until the header's avtp_timestamp is reached, rather than invoking the handler synchronously. TC18 §11.2 (TC18.txt:1093), §11.2.1 (TC18.txt:1140), §11.4.3 (TC18.txt:1976) and §12.9.2 (TC18.txt:3250-3251). Supersedes REQ-UDP-010's documented immediate-dispatch non-goal.

requirements.title: KindLong with mtv=0 is the sole routing signal for a conditional or cancel envelope
requirements.text: request.Dispatcher.Submit shall treat an acf.Message as a conditional/cancel envelope exactly when Kind == acf.KindLong && !MTV, and shall dispatch every acf.KindShort message and every acf.KindLong message with MTV set to the wrapped Handler unchanged as a plain request. TC18 §11.2 (TC18.txt:1116-1122) and Tables 11-13 (TC18.txt:1701).

requirements.title: A standard ACF_ABB request with hs, cs or err set is rejected
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The receive path shall reject an acf.KindShort standard request whose HS, CS or FlagError bit is set; TC18 Table 4 fixes mtv, rsv, hs, cs and err to zero for every standard request. acf.Message.HS and .CS round-trip but have no consumer today. TC18 §11.2.1 Table 4 (TC18.txt:1156-1167).

requirements.title: A conditional request's request_type occupies message_timestamp byte 0 with the Table 5 codes
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A conditional request shall carry its request_type as the first octet of acf.Message.Timestamp with the values TC18 Table 5 assigns — 0x0F/0x8F compound, 0x0B/0x8B compound wait, 0x0E/0x8E triggered, 0x01 chained, 0x0A timed — not as a leading Body byte with this package's own iota values. TC18 §11.2.2 Table 5 (TC18.txt:1187-1199). Tracked as go-RCP-F1 in ROADMAP.md.

requirements.title: Safety-request tagging uses the Table 5 0x8x codes
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The safety-request variants shall encode as request_type 0x8F (compound), 0x8B (compound wait) and 0x8E (triggered) — the base Table 5 code with bit 7 set — rather than request.KindCompoundSafety=0x81, KindCompoundWaitSafety=0x82 and KindTriggeredSafety=0x83. The safety *behaviour* is already required by REQ-REQ-022..025; only the wire values differ. TC18 §11.2.2 (TC18.txt:1189-1191).

requirements.title: A conditional request reaching an endpoint with no conditional support is answered UNSUPPORTED_CMD
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — udp.Router.Route shall answer a KindLong/mtv=0 conditional request addressed to a handler that does not implement conditional handling with an error response carrying udp.ErrorCodeUnsupportedCommand, rather than passing the envelope through as an opaque endpoint payload. TC18 §11.2.2.1 (TC18.txt:1204-1205), §11.2.2.2 (TC18.txt:1300-1301), §11.2.2.3 (TC18.txt:1409-1410) and §11.2.2.4 (TC18.txt:1497-1498).

requirements.title: Compound requests use the cmp_start_state / cmp_next_state state-transition model
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.EncodeCompound/DecodeCompound shall carry cmp_sequencer, cmp_start_state and cmp_next_state; the request shall start when the addressed sequencer's state equals cmp_start_state (or in any state when cmp_start_state is 0, unless the sequencer is disabled) and on completion shall set the sequencer to cmp_next_state when non-zero. The current request.Conditional comparison model is this package's own. TC18 §11.2.2.1 Figure 8 / Table 6 (TC18.txt:1206-1215, 1249-1281).

requirements.title: Every conditional request honours its exec_delay in units of ep_delay_time
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.Dispatcher.Pump shall delay a matched compound, compound-wait, triggered or chained ticket by its encoded *_exec_delay multiplied by the endpoint's configured ep_delay_time (1/10/20/50 us per TC18 §13.2 Table 28), and shall still execute the request once that delay expires even if the sequencer state changed meanwhile. No exec_delay field exists today. TC18 §11.2.2.1 Table 6 (TC18.txt:1262-1265), Table 7 (TC18.txt:1369-1372), Table 8 (TC18.txt:1459-1461), Table 9 (TC18.txt:1550-1551).

requirements.title: A repetition counter controls re-arming and request-storage removal
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.Dispatcher shall re-arm a conditional ticket after each execution while its *_repetitions field is non-zero, decrementing it by one per execution, shall never decrement the reserved infinite value 0xFFFF, and shall remove the ticket once the count reaches zero at end of execution. TC18 §11.2.2.1 Table 6 (TC18.txt:1266-1269) and §12.9.3 (TC18.txt:3281-3286).

requirements.title: A starvation-prone repetitive wildcard compound request is diagnosed
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.EncodeCompound should diagnose an encoding combining cmp_start_state == 0, a non-zero cmp_repetitions and cmp_exec_delay == 0 — the combination TC18 warns will hinder execution of other compound requests and of lower-priority requests. This is a SHOULD-strength clause and is recorded here so the corpus is complete rather than because a fix is planned. TC18 §11.2.2.1 (TC18.txt:1213-1215).

requirements.title: A compound-wait condition is evaluated over the endpoint's output state under evt, gated by cs
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.Dispatcher shall resolve a KindCompoundWait ticket by comparing the request's byte_msg_payload against the addressed endpoint's current output state under the comparison acf.Message evt[2:0] selects, checking once immediately when CS is clear and only after the next endpoint output-state change when CS is set. The current implementation compares a sequencer register and never touches the endpoint. TC18 §11.2.2.2 (TC18.txt:1303, 1306-1310, 1336-1339).

requirements.title: Triggered requests carry trigger_signal_nr and trigger_threshold at full source-EP width
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.EncodeTriggered/DecodeTriggered shall carry trigger_source_ep at its full 11-bit avtp.ByteBusID width plus trigger_signal_nr, trigger_threshold, trigger_exec_delay and trigger_repetitions, and the Dispatcher shall execute only after trigger_threshold + 1 events of the named signal number. Today the source is truncated to one byte and the threshold is fixed at zero. TC18 §11.2.2.3 Figure 10 / Table 8 (TC18.txt:1454-1461).

requirements.title: A chain links successive messages within one AVTPDU and never spans two
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A chained request shall link one acf.Message in an acf.Frame.Messages slice to its immediate predecessor in the same frame, deferring execution until that predecessor finalizes, and a chain shall never span two AVTPDUs. The current model packs a segment list inside a single message's Body. TC18 §11.2.2.4 (TC18.txt:1499-1501, 1521).

requirements.title: A leading chained request in an AVTPDU is ignored and every chain member is answered CHAIN_ERROR
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When the first message of an AVTPDU is a chained request there is no predecessor to chain to: the server shall execute no request in that chain and shall emit one error response per chained request carrying udp.ErrorCodeChainError, unless suppressed by endpoint configuration. TC18 §11.2.2.4 (TC18.txt:1518-1520).

requirements.title: A chained request's cs bit selects continue-on-error versus CHAIN_ABORTED
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.Dispatcher shall execute a chained request whose acf.Message.CS is clear even when its predecessor returned an error, and shall skip it and every remaining link — answering udp.ErrorCodeChainAborted — only when CS is set. The current implementation is unconditionally fail-fast, i.e. the cs=1 branch applied always. TC18 §11.2.2.4 Table 9 (TC18.txt:1555-1560).

requirements.title: A chain repeats under its first request's repetition count
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.Dispatcher shall re-execute an entire chain from its first request once per repetition remaining on that first request's repetition count, and shall remove every request in the chain from request storage when no repetitions remain. TC18 §11.2.2.4 (TC18.txt:1522-1524).

requirements.title: A still-executing chained request is not restarted by a repeated predecessor completion
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.Dispatcher shall ignore a predecessor's repeat finalization while the chained successor has not itself finalized, never starting that successor a second time concurrently. TC18 §11.2.2.4 (TC18.txt:1525-1526).

requirements.title: Non-zero reserved bits in a chained request are rejected
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.DecodeChained shall reject a chained request whose TC18 Figure 11 reserved fields (following request_type and following chain_exec_delay) are non-zero. Depends on the Figure 11 layout being adopted at all. TC18 §11.2.2.4 Table 9 (TC18.txt:1549, 1552).

requirements.title: A timed request carries a 48-bit gPTP presentation_time in message_timestamp
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.EncodeTimed/DecodeTimed shall write request_type 0x0A followed by a 48-bit presentation_time in acf.Message.Timestamp, with presentation_time = (AS_sec x 10^9 + AS_ns) mod 2^48 in gPTP nanoseconds, and Dispatcher.Pump shall compare against that same domain including its ~3.25-day rollover. Today an arbitrary caller-chosen 64-bit monotonic microsecond value is carried in Body. TC18 §11.2.2.5 Figure 12 / Table 10 (TC18.txt:1590-1591, 1615-1616).

requirements.title: Non-zero reserved bits in a timed request are rejected
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.DecodeTimed shall reject a timed request whose TC18 Figure 12 reserved field (between request_type and presentation_time[47:32]) is non-zero. TC18 §11.2.2.5 Table 10 (TC18.txt:1614).

requirements.title: A timed request with hs or cs set is rejected with UNSUPPORTED_CMD
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The receive path shall answer a timed request whose acf.Message.HS or CS bit is set with an error response carrying udp.ErrorCodeUnsupportedCommand. TC18 §11.2.2.5 Table 10 (TC18.txt:1628-1629).

requirements.title: A timed request's own presentation_time overrides the enclosing TSCF avtp_timestamp
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When a request_type 0x0A timed request arrives under a timestamped (TSCF) avtp.Header, the schedule shall be taken from the request's own 48-bit presentation_time and the header's Timestamp shall be ignored. TC18 §11.2.2.5 (TC18.txt:1646-1647).

requirements.title: Timed requests are rejected with GPTP_FAIL when synchronization is not established
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — udp.Router shall distinguish 'time synchronization not supported' (TC18 §11.1 TC18.txt:1074: drop the AVTPDU, send no response) from 'supported but not currently established' (send an error response carrying udp.ErrorCodeGPTPFailure), applying the latter to both a request_type 0x0A timed request and a TSCF-headed request. udp.ErrorCodeGPTPFailure is defined and golden-tested today but produced by no code path. TC18 §11.2.2.5 (TC18.txt:1651-1652) and §12.9.6 Table 27 (TC18.txt:3438).

requirements.title: A configurable scheduling horizon rejects an over-distant presentation_time
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — udp.Router may expose a maximum scheduling horizon and answer a timed request beyond it with udp.ErrorCodePresentationTimeTooFarInFuture. The clause is explicitly optional per TC18 ('may reject ... which is implementation dependent'); the entry exists because udp.ErrorCodePresentationTimeTooFarInFuture is exported, accepted by ErrorCode.Valid and golden-tested while no code path produces it. TC18 §11.2.2.5 (TC18.txt:1649-1650).

requirements.title: Loss of time synchronization does not stall already-accepted timed requests
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — An already-accepted timed or TSCF-scheduled ticket shall continue to be evaluated and executed against the free-running local clock after time synchronization is lost; only newly arriving timed requests are rejected. There is no clock abstraction today — Dispatcher.Pump takes the time from its caller. TC18 §11.2.2.5 (TC18.txt:1654-1656).

requirements.title: Cancelling a request cancels its chained successors
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When a cancellation finalizes a ticket, request.Dispatcher shall also finalize every pending ticket chained as a successor of it. go-RCP models a chain as one ticket holding a segment list, so there is no inter-ticket successor relation to follow. TC18 §11.2.3 (TC18.txt:1674-1675).

requirements.title: Every cancelled request produces a REQUEST_CANCELED error response on the wire
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — For every TicketID request.Dispatcher.Pump reports as finalized by a cancellation, the server shall emit an error response correlated to that ticket's original TransactionNum carrying acf.FlagError and udp.ErrorCodeRequestCancelled. The error-code mapping exists but Pump's finalized-ID return value is consumed by no caller, so a cancelled request is left with no reply. TC18 §11.2.3 (TC18.txt:1675-1676).

requirements.title: Cancellation never aborts a request already under execution
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.Dispatcher's cancellation kinds shall finalize only tickets in StateQueued or StateStarted, never one in StateExecuting, and Kind.IsCancellation's documented contract shall state that bound rather than claiming Executing tickets are cleared. The current matcher accepts any non-finalized ticket; synchronous execution inside Pump makes the violation unreachable today but the stated contract is wrong. TC18 §11.2.3 (TC18.txt:1673-1674).

requirements.title: Cancellation clears only tickets received on the cancelling request's own stream
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.Dispatcher's three cancellation kinds shall finalize only tickets whose recorded requester avtp.StreamID equals that of the cancellation request itself. All three matchers ignore the requester today, so a cancellation from one stream clears another stream's pending tickets. TC18 §11.2.3.1 (TC18.txt:1680), §11.2.3.2 (TC18.txt:1734) and §11.2.3.3 (TC18.txt:1793, 1796).

requirements.title: A cancellation request_type occupies the first byte of the message_timestamp field
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A cancellation request shall be an acf.KindLong message with MTV false whose Timestamp field's leading octet is the TC18 request_type — 0x05 clear-all, 0x06 clear-all-non-safestate, 0x07 clear-single followed by the clear_transaction_num. The request.Kind byte at Body[0] (values 6/7/8) is this implementation's own encoding. TC18 §11.2.3.1 Figure 13/Table 11 (TC18.txt:1681,1704), §11.2.3.2 Figure 14/Table 12 (TC18.txt:1735,1759), §11.2.3.3 Figure 15/Table 13 (TC18.txt:1794,1819).

requirements.title: A cancellation request with non-zero evt[2:0], hs or cs is rejected with UNSUPPORTED_CMD
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.Dispatcher.Submit shall reject a cancellation-kind request whose evt[2:0] is non-zero or whose HS or CS is set, with an error udp.errorCodeFor renders as udp.ErrorCodeUnsupportedCommand; evt[3] (acknowledge-requested) remains permitted. TC18 §11.2.3.1 (TC18.txt:1681) and §11.2.3.2 Table 12 (TC18.txt:1774-1775).

requirements.title: Reserved bits of a cancellation request's message_timestamp field must be zero
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — Decoding a cancellation request shall reject it when any bit TC18 Tables 11-13 mark reserved within the repurposed message_timestamp field is non-zero. Unreachable today because that field is treated as an opaque uint64. TC18 §11.2.3.1 Table 11 (TC18.txt:1705), Table 12 (TC18.txt:1760), Table 13 (TC18.txt:1820).

requirements.title: The optional clear-all-non-safestate cancellation is request_type 0x06
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — If go-RCP implements TC18's optional enhanced cancellation, request_type 0x06 shall clear every non-safety ticket received on the same stream — the semantic request.Dispatcher.PurgeNonSafety already implements but which is reachable only from the watchdog, not from any wire request — and request.KindCancelSequencer shall be documented as a go-RCP extension with no TC18 counterpart rather than as one of the two optional variants. TC18 §11.2.3.2 (TC18.txt:1733-1736) and §12.2 (TC18.txt:2038).

requirements.title: A clear-single cancellation matching no transaction returns REQUEST_NOT_FOUND
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.Dispatcher's clear-single cancellation shall finalize with an error udp.errorCodeFor renders as udp.ErrorCodeRequestNotFound when no pending ticket on the requester's stream carries the requested clear_transaction_num, rather than returning a success response reporting zero cancellations. TC18 §11.2.3.3 (TC18.txt:1837-1838).

requirements.title: A successful clear-single cancellation response carries an empty body
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The clear-single success response shall have a nil or empty Body; the cancelled-count body EncodeCancelResponse produces is this implementation's own addition. TC18 §11.2.3.3 (TC18.txt:1838).

requirements.title: Response evt[3:0] carries TC18 Table 15's response coding
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — acf shall expose the response-side interpretation of evt[3:0] — 0x0 simple/data/error response, 0x1..0x8 the multi-response counter rolling over from 0x8 to 0x1, 0x9..0xE reserved, 0xF acknowledge — as a classifier distinct from ClassifyEVT's request-side Table 30 rows, and shall reject a decoded response whose evt[3:0] falls in 0x9..0xE. Every response builder leaves EVT at zero today. TC18 §11.3 Table 15 (TC18.txt:1876-1880) and §12.9.4 (TC18.txt:3373-3377).

requirements.title: A request with evt[3] set receives an evt[3:0]=0xF acknowledge
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When acf.Message.EVTAckRequested reports true, the server shall emit an acknowledge with evt[3:0] = 0xF and an empty body on successful filing into the endpoint's request storage (err=0), and with err=1 plus an error-code body when the request is rejected, separate from and preceding the request's own response. EVTAckRequested has no non-test caller in the repository. TC18 §11.3.1 (TC18.txt:1908-1911), §13.5 (TC18.txt:3673), §12.9.1 (TC18.txt:3205-3206) and §12.9.5 (TC18.txt:3384-3387).

requirements.title: A successful write response carries no byte_msg_payload
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A response to a request with op = 1 (acf.FlagWrite) and evt[3:0] < 0x9 shall have an empty Body. Endpoint packages that echo the written value back conflict with this clause, and so do the existing requirements that mandate the echo (REQ-CANEP-008, REQ-LINEP-005, REQ-SPI-006, REQ-I2C-006); resolving it needs a deliberate decision, not a silent change. TC18 §11.3.2 (TC18.txt:1915-1916).

requirements.title: An untimestamped response is emitted as ACF_ABB, not ACF_GBB
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A response carrying no capture timestamp shall be acf.KindShort (ACF_ABB, acf_msg_type 0x0E) regardless of the requesting message's own Kind. Every response builder copies req.Kind through today, so a response to a conditional or cancellation request goes out as ACF_GBB carrying an all-zero, invalid message_timestamp. TC18 §11.3 (TC18.txt:1864) and §11.4.2 (TC18.txt:1965-1966).

requirements.title: Every response sets rsp, echoes op, and leaves hs and cs zero
requirements.text: Every response go-RCP emits shall carry acf.FlagResponse, the same op bit (FlagRead/FlagWrite) as its request, and HS and CS false. TC18 §11.3 Table 15 (TC18.txt:1881-1885).

requirements.title: Every error response carries a valid Table 27 error code as its leading payload byte
requirements.text: A response carrying acf.FlagError shall have a non-empty Body whose leading byte is a udp.ErrorCode for which ErrorCode.Valid reports true. TC18 §11.3.4 (TC18.txt:1925-1926) and §12.9.6 (TC18.txt:3410-3411).

requirements.title: avtp_timestamp is derived from gPTP seconds and nanoseconds modulo 2^32
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — avtp shall provide a conversion from a gPTP (seconds, nanoseconds) pair to the 32-bit Header.Timestamp as (AS_sec x 10^9 + AS_ns) mod 2^32, so a caller cannot supply an arbitrarily-scaled value; the field rolls over roughly every 4.29 s. TC18 §11.4.1 (TC18.txt:1952-1954).

requirements.title: message_timestamp is derived from gPTP seconds and nanoseconds modulo 2^64
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — acf shall provide a conversion from a gPTP (seconds, nanoseconds) pair to the 64-bit Message.Timestamp as (AS_sec x 10^9 + AS_ns) mod 2^64, and that shall be the only supported way to populate the field with a valid (MTV=1) capture timestamp. TC18 §11.4.1 (TC18.txt:1955-1957).

requirements.title: Response and acknowledge timestamping are separately selectable per endpoint
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The endpoint register map shall carry two independent per-endpoint flags selecting whether responses and whether acknowledges are timestamped; when a flag is clear the corresponding message shall be acf.KindShort with no timestamp slot, when set it shall be acf.KindLong with MTV true. No timestamp selection exists anywhere in regmap. TC18 §11.4.2 (TC18.txt:1964-1966), §12.9.4 (TC18.txt:3369-3370) and §13.7 Table 32 (TC18.txt:3924-3934).

requirements.title: An acknowledge's message_timestamp is the moment of acceptance into the request storage
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When acknowledge timestamping is enabled, the acknowledge's Message.Timestamp shall be the time request.Dispatcher.Submit admitted the ticket, not the time it executed or the time the acknowledge was transmitted. TC18 §11.4.2 (TC18.txt:1967-1968).

requirements.title: A read response's message_timestamp is the physical-interface capture instant
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When response timestamping is enabled, a read response's Message.Timestamp shall be the time the reported input signal was captured at the endpoint's physical interface, not the time the response was built; endpoint Transport interfaces would have to surface a capture instant. TC18 §11.4.2 (TC18.txt:1969-1970).

requirements.title: The RC Server always replies with an untimed (NTSCF) AVTPDU header
requirements.text: Every AVTPDU the server transmits shall carry an untimed (NTSCF, subtype 0x82) avtp.Header with Timed false; a capture timestamp is conveyed only via ACF_GBB's message_timestamp, never by a TSCF header. TC18 §11.4.3 (TC18.txt:1979-1980).

requirements.title: An internal clock may be synchronized to the system clock as a receiving clock
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — An RC Server may synchronize an internal clock to a system clock using IEEE 802.1AS (gPTP), acting as a receiving clock. Not implemented and not claimed: udp.NewRouter takes a static caller-supplied timeSyncSupported flag, explicitly documented as not a live check. Recorded because every §11.4 timestamp requirement depends on it. TC18 §11.4 (TC18.txt:1943-1946) and §12.2 (TC18.txt:2021-2027).

requirements.title: The RC Server exposes status and debug information for itself and its endpoints
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap.RegisterMap shall carry a readable status/debug region for the server and for each declared endpoint, so udp.ErrorCodeEPError has the ep_status detail register its own documentation already promises. No status-shaped block exists. TC18 §12.1 (TC18.txt:2010) and §12.9.6 Table 27 (TC18.txt:3424).

requirements.title: A set configuration lock rejects every write to a lockable register
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When regmap.GeneralBlock.ConfigLock is non-zero, the server's configuration write paths shall return regmap.ErrRegisterLocked and leave the map unchanged, independently of lifecycle state and of root-client status. ConfigLock round-trips on the wire but no write path consults it. TC18 §12.1 (TC18.txt:2009) and §12.7.5 Table 18 (TC18.txt:2551-2553).

requirements.title: A conformant RC Server implements TC18's four mandatory features
requirements.text: A server shall support NTSCF header processing, standard request handling, an endpoint at regmap.EP0, and the clear-all-requests cancellation request — the four features TC18 makes mandatory for every compliant RC Server, none of which may be left unregistered. TC18 §12.2 (TC18.txt:2014-2019).

requirements.title: Optional-feature bundles are advertised consistently
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap shall define named constants for each GeneralBlock.Options bit and validate the bundles TC18 defines: the compound-request bit requires at least four sequencer state registers, and the time-synchronization bit requires TSCF processing, gPTP, timed requests and timestamped acknowledges and responses. Options is a raw byte with no constants and no validation today. TC18 §12.2 (TC18.txt:2021-2038), §12.7.5 Table 18 (TC18.txt:2554-2560) and §12.10 (TC18.txt:3471).

requirements.title: A server starts in the lifecycle state it was configured in
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The server package shall provide a constructor restoring a persisted lifecycle.LifecycleState together with its register map, so a cold-started server resumes the state it was configured in and enforces that state's locks from its first call, rather than always starting at StateUnconfigured. TC18 §12.3 (TC18.txt:2059-2062) and §12.4.1 (TC18.txt:2289-2292).

requirements.title: svr_lifecycle_state is a register that reads and drives lifecycle transitions
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The encoded register map shall carry an 8-bit svr_lifecycle_state field encoding 0x00 HW_UNCONFIGURED, 0x55 HW_CONFIGURED and 0xAA RCP_CONFIGURED, readable through a discovery read, and a write of one of those values through EP0 shall invoke the corresponding transition guard. Lifecycle transitions are Go-API-only today and lifecycle.LifecycleState uses iota values 0/1/2, discarding TC18's deliberately high-Hamming-distance encodings. TC18 §12.3.1 (TC18.txt:2167,2186,2199) and §13.7.1.2 Table 33 (TC18.txt:3990-3992).

requirements.title: Advancing to HW_CONFIGURED enforces both plausibility checks
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The HW_UNCONFIGURED to HW_CONFIGURED transition shall be rejected, leaving the state unchanged, when any endpoint with ep_used set has no entry in the pin map, or when the request-queue configuration has not been set for such an endpoint. Only the converse pin-map direction is checked today, and the queue check runs at the later transition. TC18 §12.3.1.1 (TC18.txt:2169-2174).

requirements.title: Advancing to RCP_CONFIGURED enforces the stream-association plausibility checks
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The HW_CONFIGURED to RCP_CONFIGURED transition shall be rejected when any used endpoint has no stream_id/byte_bus_id association, when a configured stream has no byte_bus_id, or when a configured response stream is assigned to no request stream. None of the three is performed, because the association table those checks operate on does not exist in regmap. TC18 §12.3.1.2 (TC18.txt:2190-2196).

requirements.title: Demotion out of HW_CONFIGURED is refused while any endpoint is not idle
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — server.Server.DemoteToUnconfigured shall return an EPs-not-idle error, leaving the lifecycle state unchanged, when any declared endpoint still has a pending or in-flight request; endpoint idleness shall be an interrogable predicate. No such predicate exists. TC18 §12.3 Figure 16 (TC18.txt:2119, 2129-2131).

requirements.title: Lifecycle-transition failures map onto defined Table 27 error codes
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — Each lifecycle-transition rejection shall be rendered as a defined udp.ErrorCode rather than the unclassified fallback: DISCOVERY_STREAM_OCCUPIED, HW_CFG_INCONSISTENT, RCP_CFG_INCONSISTENT, LOCKED_CONFIG_ACCESS and EPs_NOT_IDLE. None of Figure 16's five names appears in Table 27, so the mapping chosen shall be recorded as a resolution of that spec-internal inconsistency. TC18 §12.3 Figure 16 (TC18.txt:2075,2087,2108,2113,2131) versus §12.9.6 Table 27 (TC18.txt:3414-3446).

requirements.title: An unconfigured server silently drops every request but an EP0 discovery read
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — While the server is in StateUnconfigured, the receive path shall emit no reply at all for any request that is not an ACF_ABB request to regmap.EP0 on the assigned discovery stream, and for any request on an unknown stream_id/byte_bus_id combination. udp.Router never consults the server's lifecycle state and answers an unknown endpoint with an error response. TC18 §12.3.1.1 (TC18.txt:2164) and §12.3 Figure 16 (TC18.txt:2075-2077, 2101-2105).

requirements.title: TSCF and ACF_GBB requests are dropped in the two pre-configured lifecycle states
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The receive path shall drop without reply every request carrying a timestamped (TSCF) header and every acf.KindLong (ACF_GBB) request while the server is in StateUnconfigured or StateHWLocked, independently of the router's time-sync capability flag. Today a TSCF request is dropped only when time sync is unsupported, and ACF_GBB is rejected only on the EP0 discovery-read path. TC18 §12.3.1.1 (TC18.txt:2162) and §12.3.1.2 (TC18.txt:2180-2181).

requirements.title: Write requests are accepted only from unicast frames
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The request-admission path shall carry the frame's destination MAC and reject any request with acf.FlagWrite set whose destination MAC has the group bit set, in every lifecycle state; reads including broadcast discovery are unaffected. No code inspects the destination address, which never reaches the admission path. TC18 §12.3.1.1 (TC18.txt:2166), §12.3.1.2 (TC18.txt:2181), §12.3.1.3 (TC18.txt:2223).

requirements.title: EP0 writes while HW_CONFIGURED admit the active discovery-stream claimant
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — While the server is in StateHWLocked, a write via EP0 to another endpoint's configuration shall be accepted from the stream holding the active discovery-stream configuration claim as well as from the configured root client; in StateFullyConfigured it remains root-client-only. WriteEP0 is root-only in every state today, so a discovery-only configuration flow cannot write endpoint configuration. TC18 §12.3.1.2 (TC18.txt:2184) and §12.3.1.3 (TC18.txt:2224).

requirements.title: Only configuration requests reach non-EP0 endpoints while HW_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The receive path shall drop without reply any request addressed to a byte_bus_id other than regmap.EP0 whose evt[2:0] is not 111b (configuration) while the server is in StateHWLocked. TC18 §12.3.1.2 (TC18.txt:2185).

requirements.title: A disabled endpoint queues operational requests and executes only configuration requests
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — While an endpoint's ep_enable bit is clear it shall execute only evt[2:0]=111b configuration requests; every operational request shall be stored in that endpoint's request storage without execution, an acknowledge shall still be sent if requested, and the stored requests shall begin executing in arrival order when ep_enable is set. There is no ep_enable field in the functional block and no per-endpoint enable gate in the dispatcher. TC18 §12.3.1.3 (TC18.txt:2218-2221) and §13.1 (TC18.txt:3509-3511).

requirements.title: A hot start checks network availability and reports the wake source
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — On a hot start the server shall enable the network interface, check availability, initiate a network wake if unavailable, and once available send a repetitive response to the original sleep request carrying a wake message and the wake-up source, on the responder stream configured for that sleep request. wakeup.WakeHandshake carries no wake source and powerstate.Driver targets a construction-time stream. TC18 §12.4.1 (TC18.txt:2296-2305).

requirements.title: The wake-handshake repetition interval is honoured
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — powerstate.Driver shall pace successive wake-handshake transmissions at wakeup.Config.WakeHandshakeIntervalMillis using an injectable clock. The field is validated non-zero and round-trips on the wire, but no code reads it for timing; repetition rate is left entirely to the caller's Pump cadence. TC18 §12.4.1 (TC18.txt:2300-2301).

requirements.title: Acknowledging the wake handshake re-enables endpoints and response queues
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — On reception of a valid message from the sleep-requesting client, the server shall re-enable every used endpoint and every configured response queue, including heartbeat-configured queues, in addition to discarding pending handshake repeats. TC18 §12.4.1 (TC18.txt:2301-2303).

requirements.title: A sleep or standby request is rejected while wake events, busy endpoints or queued responses remain
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — wakeup.Endpoint shall reject a request targeting PowerSleep or PowerStandBy, without changing state and with an error udp.errorCodeFor renders as udp.ErrorCodeRequestCancelled, when the wake-up event register wup_status is not cleared, when any declared endpoint is not idle, or when any responder queue holds a message pending transmission. None of the three predicates exists. TC18 §12.5 (TC18.txt:2327-2332).

requirements.title: A wake event racing a sleep request aborts the transition
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — If an event configured as a wake-up source occurs during the processing of a sleep request, the request shall not be executed and the server shall not enter sleep mode. The transition is applied immediately under the mutex with no re-check. TC18 §12.5 (TC18.txt:2325-2326).

requirements.title: Standby is request-only while sleep also accepts a TC14/TC10 network request
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — wakeup.Endpoint shall expose a network-initiated sleep entry point distinct from a request, applying the identical rejection conditions and reporting to its caller whether TC14/TC10 LPS may be signalled; PowerStandBy shall remain reachable only via an RC Server request. No TC14/TC10 ingress or PHY LPS hook exists. TC18 §12.5 (TC18.txt:2318-2319, 2336-2337).

requirements.title: The power-state change is committed only after its response has been sent
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — wakeup.Endpoint shall not apply a PowerSleep or PowerStandBy transition until the corresponding response has been handed to the transport, so a failed transmission leaves the server in PowerNormal. The current order is inverted: the state changes before the response is built. TC18 §12.5 (TC18.txt:2334-2335).

requirements.title: The first discovery request assigns the discovery stream
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When the server is in StateUnconfigured or StateHWLocked and no active claim is held, handling a discovery request shall establish the configuration claim for the requesting stream as a side effect of answering it, so that stream is thereafter the only one from which configuration requests are accepted. Today the claim is established only by a separate explicit call. TC18 §12.6 (TC18.txt:2356-2358).

requirements.title: The discovery-stream timeout is the specified svr_discovery_timeout default
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — discovery.DefaultConfigurationClaimTimeout shall be 20 ms — the svr_discovery_timeout default of 20000 microseconds — and the live value shall be carried in the register map as a 16-bit microsecond field kept in agreement with the configured timeout. The current default is 30 s, explicitly documented as this package's own reasoned value rather than a transcription. TC18 §12.6 (TC18.txt:2357-2359) and §13.7.1.2 Table 33 (TC18.txt:3993-3995).

requirements.title: Configuration requests from a stream other than the discovery claimant are rejected
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — While a discovery-stream configuration claim is active, the server's configuration write paths shall reject a requester that is neither the claimant nor the configured root client; the read half shall remain unrestricted, since TC18 requires every discovery request to be answered with the server_config map. The claim is consulted by no configuration method today. TC18 §12.6 (TC18.txt:2359-2361).

requirements.title: A discovery request is validated against Table 16's full field profile
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — Handling a discovery request shall additionally require sv = 1b (avtp.Header.StreamIDValid), unique_id = 0x0000 (avtp.StreamID suffix zero) and evt = 0000b, dropping without reply any request that violates them. Only the NTSCF, ACF_ABB, byte_bus_id-zero and op=read constraints are checked today. TC18 §12.6.1 Table 16 (TC18.txt:2370-2382).

requirements.title: A discovery request framed as ACF_GBB is dropped without reply
requirements.text: Handling a discovery request shall return discovery.ErrDiscoveryRequestIsACFGBB and no register-map bytes when the request is acf.KindLong, and udp.Router.Route shall render that error as a silent drop rather than a wire-level error response. TC18 §12.6.1 Table 16 (TC18.txt:2367).

requirements.title: A discovery response is truncated to the request's read_size
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The discovery response body shall be the encoded register map from address 0x0000 truncated to the request's read_size, so acf_msg_length never exceeds it. The current path returns the whole encoded map because the discovery handler never receives the acf.Message and so cannot see ReadSizeOrSegment. TC18 §12.6.2 (TC18.txt:2402-2403) and Table 17 (TC18.txt:2422-2423).

requirements.title: A discovery response uses the server's own stream_id and the requester's streamMAC as destination
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A discovery response shall carry stream_id = localMAC + unique_id 0x0000, be framed with destination MAC equal to the request's stream_id MAC and source MAC equal to the server's device MAC, and carry no VLAN tag. The response builder sets no avtp.Header and no code derives the destination from the request. TC18 §12.6.2 Table 17 (TC18.txt:2418-2419, 2432-2435).

requirements.title: Only unconditional standard requests reach EP0 before full configuration
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — While the server is in StateUnconfigured, or in StateHWLocked with no valid stream_id/byte_bus_id combination configured, EP0 shall reject any request whose kind is other than the unconditional standard kind with an error rendered as udp.ErrorCodeRequestRejected. That code is defined but reachable from no path today. TC18 §12.7 (TC18.txt:2454-2457).

requirements.title: Endpoint-direct configuration is lifecycle-gated and ends for the discovery stream at RCP_CONFIGURED
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — An endpoint-direct configuration request shall be accepted only in StateFullyConfigured, or in StateHWLocked when the requester's stream_id/byte_bus_id combination is configured for that endpoint, and shall otherwise be dropped without reply; in StateFullyConfigured a discovery-stream configuration claim shall be refused while discovery reads continue to be answered. The configuration write paths perform no lifecycle check at all. TC18 §12.7 (TC18.txt:2458-2459), §12.7.2 (TC18.txt:2488-2489), §12.7.3 (TC18.txt:2493-2494), §12.7.4 (TC18.txt:2498-2500).

requirements.title: EP_func relative address 0x00 exposes the endpoint's EP_LEN
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The first byte of every endpoint's EP_func block, as returned by a configuration read at relative start address 0x00, shall be that endpoint's EP_LEN. Today the block length is carried in a separate prefix written outside the block, so relative address 0x00 returns configuration data instead. The overrun rule (a payload whose length plus start address exceeds EP_LEN is ignored) is already covered by REQ-RCS-032. TC18 §12.7.1 (TC18.txt:2482-2484).

requirements.title: A configuration request is ACF_ABB with evt=111b and zeroed pad, mtv and rsv
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A request carrying a configuration access shall be acf.KindShort with evt[2:0] = 111b and zeroed pad/mtv/rsv fields, and the configuration path shall reject an ACF_GBB-framed or mtv-set configuration request rather than decoding its body as a §12.7.1 access. REQ-EVT-007 covers the body codec and REQ-RCS-032 the addressing; the header profile is unasserted. TC18 §12.7.1 Figure 18 (TC18.txt:2468-2479).

requirements.title: The general block carries the network, PHY, time-synch and security configuration pointers
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap.GeneralBlock shall carry eight further 16-bit read-only registers at offsets 0x0030-0x003F — network-interface, physical-layer, time-synch and security configuration pointer/capacity pairs — and shall round-trip them; a zero pointer means the corresponding feature is not supported. generalBlockLen is 0x30 today and the encoder stops at 0x2F. TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 (TC18.txt:2633-2661).

requirements.title: Reserved general-block registers always read as zero
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap.EncodeRegisterMap shall force the reserved registers at 0x0017, 0x0022-0x0023 and 0x002B to zero regardless of the stored GeneralBlock, so a client-supplied whole-map write can never cause a reserved register to read non-zero. The decoder copies whatever bytes arrive and the encoder does not force them. TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 (TC18.txt:2562, 2599).

requirements.title: The pin-mapping table is bounded by svr_io_pin_count
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap.PinMap.Validate shall reject any PinAssignment whose Pin is greater than or equal to GeneralBlock.NumIOPins, since TC18 makes the available IO-pin count a constant read from the general register block. Validate checks uniqueness, endpoint declaration and signal-index range only. TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 (TC18.txt:2564-2566) and §12.7.6 (TC18.txt:2694-2695).

requirements.title: Configured queue memory is bounded by svr_responder_mem_size and svr_req_mem_size
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — Advancing to RCP_CONFIGURED shall reject a configuration whose total configured queue memory, in 32-bit words, exceeds GeneralBlock.MaxResponderQueueWords or MaxRequestQueueWords. Both registers round-trip but constrain nothing, and there is no per-queue queue_size register to sum. TC18 §12.7.5 Table 18 (TC18.txt:2543-2547).

requirements.title: The HW_config table encodes three bytes per IO pin, indexed by pin number
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The HW_config table shall be encoded as NumIOPins consecutive 3-byte records — hw_ep_nr, hw_ep_pin_nr, hw_pin_type — positioned by physical pin index with no length prefix, so pin n's hw_ep_nr sits at the table pointer plus 3n. The current encoding is a 2-byte entry count followed by 4-byte records carrying an explicit pin field and no pin type. TC18 §12.7.6 Table 19 (TC18.txt:2698-2718).

requirements.title: A pin assignment carries the Table 20 IO-pin property bitfield
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap.PinAssignment shall carry an 8-bit hw_pin_type encoding pull mode in bits 1:0 (float, pull-down, pull-up), output stage in bits 3:2 (input, open-drain, open-source, push-pull), drive strength in bits 5:4, a reserved bit 6 reading zero, and Schmitt-trigger enable in bit 7, with validation rejecting a set bit 6. No such field exists. TC18 §12.7.6 Table 20 (TC18.txt:2738-2760) and §12.7.6 (TC18.txt:2720-2722).

requirements.title: PWM_OUT and PWM_IN are distinct endpoint types with distinct signal counts
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap shall declare separate endpoint types for PWM_OUT (signals PWM_OUT and PWM_OUTN) and PWM_IN (signal PWM_IN) so a pin assignment naming signal index 1 on a PWM input endpoint is rejected. A single merged EndpointTypePWM carries both signal names today. TC18 §12.7.6 Table 21 (TC18.txt:2807-2810) and §13.2 Table 29 (TC18.txt:3601-3618).

requirements.title: Endpoint types outside Table 21's enumeration are marked as vendor extensions
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap.EndpointTypeWakeup has no row in TC18 Table 21's endpoint-type enumeration and shall be documented as a vendor extension assigned a value in a reserved range that cannot collide with a future TC18-assigned EP_Type. TC18 §12.7.6 Table 21 (TC18.txt:2779-2821).

requirements.title: Request-stream configuration implements the Table 22 per-stream record
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap shall carry an array of per-request-stream records of 0x18 bytes each laid out per Table 22 — rx_stream_id, rx_stream_max_request_size, rx_wd_timeout_intervall, rx_secure_channel_index, the rx_enforce_e2e / rx_enforce_seq / rx_seq_safestate_enable / rx_wd_enable / rx_wd_safestate_enable / rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable / rx_safety_measure / rx_wd_info_enable bits, rx_safestate_seqencer, rx_safe_sequencer_state, rx_ack_stream_index, rx_resp_stream_index and the reserved words — with TC18's defaults, including rx_resp_stream_index defaulting to 1 so a discovery request can be answered. regmap.StreamLimits is an invented 3-byte substitute. TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22 (TC18.txt:2843-2928).

requirements.title: A zero rx_stream_id accepts no requests
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A request stream whose rx_stream_id register is zero shall receive nothing, since zero is not a valid stream_id. TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22 (TC18.txt:2847-2851).

requirements.title: rx_enforce_seq requires a single sequence-number increment, not merely a strict increase
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When rx_enforce_seq is set, requests shall be filed for execution only if the AVTPDU sequence number increased by exactly one, and rx_seq_safestate_enable shall bring all endpoints to safe state when it did not. e2e's monotonicity check accepts any strict increase (REQ-CRC-006) and neither register exists. TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22 (TC18.txt:2868-2873).

requirements.title: rx_safety_measure selects high-impedance pins or sequencer-based safety requests
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — On safe-state entry the server shall either drive all mapped IO pins to high impedance (rx_safety_measure = 0b) or use sequencer-based safety requests (1b), as that register selects. Neither behaviour nor register exists. TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22 (TC18.txt:2883-2887).

requirements.title: rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable enters safe state on request-storage overflow
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When rx_ovrflw_safestate_enable is set, the server shall enter safe state if the request storage of any endpoint overflows. No overflow-to-safe-state path exists. TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22 (TC18.txt:2880-2882).

requirements.title: rx_wd_info_enable emits repetitive safe-state notifications
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When rx_wd_info_enable is set, the server shall send a repetitive notification while in safe state. TC18 §12.7.7 Table 22 (TC18.txt:2888-2890).

requirements.title: EP_ID_config maps (request stream, byte_bus_id) pairs to endpoints
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap shall encode an EP_ID_config table of up to EndpointMapMaxEntries 4-byte entries — Request_Stream_Index, EP_Nr and a 16-bit BBID carrying an 11-bit byte_bus_id — defaulting entry 1 to {1, 0, 0} so EP0 is reachable, treating Request_Stream_Index 0 as end-of-table, and rejecting entries not in ascending order. The section is never emitted and routing is done by an unrelated grant model. TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23 (TC18.txt:2962-2990).

requirements.title: An endpoint address preserves all eleven bits of byte_bus_id
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap's generic endpoint block shall encode avtp.ByteBusID in sixteen bits rather than truncating it to eight, since TC18 makes byte_bus_id an 11-bit field. The encoder writes a single byte today, so an endpoint above address 255 cannot survive an encode. TC18 §12.7.8 Table 23 (TC18.txt:2962-2990) and §11.2.1 Table 4.

requirements.title: Granting an endpoint to a second stream is reported as a safety-relevant condition
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap.AccessController.Grant shall expose whether the endpoint was already granted to a different stream, since TC18 recommends for safety reasons that one endpoint be used by one RC Client at a time. This is a SHOULD-strength clause; Grant currently permits unlimited streams silently. TC18 §12.7.8 (TC18.txt:2985).

requirements.title: Endpoints sharing a byte_bus_id within one stream are of the same type
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — If multiple endpoints use the same byte_bus_id inside one stream they should be of the same type; this SHOULD-strength clause cannot be checked because no EP_ID_config table exists to check against. TC18 §12.7.8 (TC18.txt:2988).

requirements.title: Max_AVTPDUsize bounds every generated AVTPDU and is validated against the MTU
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The responder-queue configuration shall carry a 16-bit Max_AVTPDUsize in quadlets, the server shall never emit an AVTPDU longer than four times that value, and advancing to RCP_CONFIGURED shall reject a configuration whose Max_AVTPDUsize would produce a frame exceeding the transport MTU. udp.MaxFrameLen is a compile-time constant, not a register. TC18 §12.7.9 (TC18.txt:3009-3011) and Table 24 (TC18.txt:3030-3032).

requirements.title: The responder-queue fragmentation threshold is derived from Max_AVTPDUsize
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The responder queue shall call fragment.Split with a maximum body derived from that queue's Max_AVTPDUsize rather than fragment.DefaultMaxSegmentBody, which is documented in the package itself as a choice and not a specification-mandated limit. TC18 §12.7.9 (TC18.txt:3012-3013).

requirements.title: flush_on_count is measured in 32-bit words and flushes inclusively
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The queue flush threshold shall count 32-bit words of queued payload rather than messages, shall default to 1 meaning immediate transmission, and on crossing the threshold the server shall transmit every queued ACF type including the one that crossed it, packed into as many AVTPDUs as Max_AVTPDUsize requires. regmap.QueueConfig.FlushThreshold counts messages and defaults to zero. TC18 §12.7.9 (TC18.txt:3014-3017) and Table 24 (TC18.txt:3035-3039).

requirements.title: Flush_time is a 16-bit microsecond register
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The queue flush-time register shall be a 16-bit value in microseconds with zero meaning flush-only-by-count, replacing regmap.QueueConfig's 32-bit millisecond field. TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24 (TC18.txt:3041-3043).

requirements.title: An expired Flush_time transmits an AVTPDU even when the queue is empty
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When a responder queue's Flush_time elapses since its last transmission the server shall emit an AVTPDU even if the queue is empty, which is the liveness heartbeat; the separate HeartbeatIntervalMillis field is a register Table 24 does not define and should be removed in favour of that behaviour. TC18 §12.7.9 (TC18.txt:3018-3021) and §13.7.1.1 (TC18.txt:3967-3970).

requirements.title: QUEUE_config is a per-responder-queue array with distinct lock classes
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap shall encode QUEUE_config as an array of 0x0A-byte records — STREAM_UID, Max_AVTPDUsize, queue_size, flush_on_count, Flush_time — one per configurable response stream, gating STREAM_UID, flush_on_count and Flush_time on the configuration lock (R/W+) while gating Max_AVTPDUsize and queue_size on lifecycle state (R/W*). RegisterMap.Queues is a single global QueueConfig with one uniform lock. TC18 §12.7.9 Table 24 (TC18.txt:3025-3048).

requirements.title: Sequencer state registers read 1 after reset, not 0
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.NewSequencer shall initialise every sequencer state register to 1, so Get returns 1 for a never-advanced SequencerID; TC18 states that upon power-on reset all sequencer state values are set to 1 and Table 25 gives Seq_state a default of 1. The current bank starts every register at zero, and REQ-REQ-004's 'starting at zero' clause codifies that deviation. TC18 §12.7.10 (TC18.txt:3068-3069), Table 25 (TC18.txt:3080-3081) and §12.10 (TC18.txt:3466-3468).

requirements.title: SEQUENCER_config exposes sequencer state and client binding through the register map
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap shall encode a SEQUENCER_config table of 2-byte records — Seq_state (8-bit R/W, reset value 1, zero meaning disabled) and Request_stream_index (8-bit R/W*) — backed by the same registers request.Sequencer uses, and shall reject a sequencer access issued by a stream other than that sequencer's Request_stream_index. The pointer is documented as always zero on encode and no section is emitted. Note also that Table 25 makes Seq_state 8-bit where request.Sequencer stores uint32. TC18 §12.7.10 Table 25 (TC18.txt:3077-3097) and §12.10 (TC18.txt:3468-3470).

requirements.title: svr_sequencers_max advertises the sequencers the server actually implements
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The server shall set GeneralBlock.NumSequencerStates to the number of sequencer state registers it provides, so a client reading the general block is not told sequencer operation is unsupported while compound requests are in fact honoured. The field is never set above zero today. TC18 §12.7.10 (TC18.txt:3071-3073) and §12.7.5 Table 18 (TC18.txt:2548-2550).

requirements.title: Product-specific configuration windows are addressable through their general-block pointers
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap shall expose the network-interface, physical-layer, time-synch and security configuration sections as opaque byte windows located at their respective general-block pointers and bounded by the matching capacity registers, round-tripping their bytes without interpreting them, with a zero pointer signalling that physical-layer configuration, time synch or security respectively is not supported. TC18 §12.7.11 (TC18.txt:3114-3119), §12.7.12 (TC18.txt:3122-3128), §12.7.13 (TC18.txt:3131-3135), §12.7.14 (TC18.txt:3138-3142).

requirements.title: A 10BASE-T1S deployment declares its PLCA transmit slots
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When the configured link is 10BASE-T1S the transport shall carry at least one configured PLCA transmit-opportunity slot in which the RC Server is allowed to send, and shall refuse to transmit when none is configured. No PLCA concept exists in the repository. TC18 §12.8.1 (TC18.txt:3162-3163).

requirements.title: MACsec-protected frames are verified and unwrapped before AVTPDU decode
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — If MACsec is enabled on an interface, the receive path shall verify and strip the SecTAG and ICV before handing the remainder to acf.DecodeFrame. This is a MAY-strength clause in TC18 and is not implemented; it is recorded because §12.7.7's rx_secure_channel_index register presumes it. TC18 §12.8.2 (TC18.txt:3168-3169).

requirements.title: A frame that is neither gPTP nor an IEEE 1722 AVTPDU is discarded
requirements.text: avtp.DecodeHeader shall return avtp.ErrUnknownSubtype for any buffer whose subtype octet is neither SubtypeNTSCF (0x82) nor SubtypeTSCF (0x05), and the receive path shall drop such a datagram without reply rather than misinterpreting it. TC18 §12.8.2 (TC18.txt:3170).

requirements.title: Fragmented requests are reassembled before dispatch
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The receive path shall pass every inbound acf.Message carrying acf.FlagMoreSegments through a fragment.Reassembler and dispatch only the reassembled message to the addressed handler. The fragment package is complete and required by REQ-FRAG-001..012 but is not wired into the server, so a non-terminal segment is routed as if it were a whole request. TC18 §12.8.2 (TC18.txt:3174).

requirements.title: Frames arriving at the minimum interpacket gap are not dropped
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The receive path shall not drop a correctly formed AVTPDU solely because it arrived at the minimum time after its predecessor. This is a PHY/driver-level property with no representation in this library. TC18 §12.8.2 (TC18.txt:3175-3176).

requirements.title: Responses and acknowledges are emitted through per-stream responder and acknowledge queues
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The server shall maintain one responder queue and one acknowledge queue per configured stream, each with its own (possibly multicast) destination address, and each endpoint's configuration shall name which queues carry its responses and acknowledges for a request received on a given stream. regmap.QueueConfig is a single global flush table and replies are sent synchronously to the sender's address. TC18 §12.9.1 (TC18.txt:3201-3204) and §12.9.4 (TC18.txt:3366-3368).

requirements.title: A frame carrying multiple ACF messages is decoded and routed message by message
requirements.text: acf.DecodeFrame shall return every ACF message present in an AVTPDU payload in wire order, and the server shall route each one individually, checking each against the addressed endpoint and emitting one reply frame carrying every response produced. TC18 §12.9.1.1 (TC18.txt:3221-3223) and §12.9.1.1 (TC18.txt:3226-3231).

requirements.title: One frame's header governs every message it carries
requirements.text: acf.Frame shall carry exactly one avtp.Header, and that header shall be passed unchanged when routing every message decoded from the frame, so a TSCF presentation time applies uniformly to all of them and a mixture of timestamped and untimestamped requests in one frame is impossible. TC18 §12.9.1.1 (TC18.txt:3224-3226).

requirements.title: Mixed request types in one frame are each dispatched under their own kind
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — Each message of a multi-message frame shall be dispatched according to its own request kind, so a frame mixing standard, triggered and compound requests executes each under its own readiness rule. Heterogeneous messages per frame decode correctly, but the request-type envelopes themselves are this repository's own layout rather than TC18 §11.2.2's. TC18 §12.9.1.1 (TC18.txt:3226-3231).

requirements.title: Table 26's per-type execution procedure governs each kind's RS/RE/RF transitions
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.Dispatcher shall implement TC18 Table 26 for each request kind: cancellation, timed and standard requests advance from request-started to request-under-execution immediately; triggered, compound and chained requests start their exec-delay timer on entering request-started and advance only once it expires and the endpoint is idle with no higher-priority request pending; a triggered request resets its trigger count on entering request-started; a compound request sets cmp_sequencer to cmp_next_state at request-finalized only if the sequencer still equals cmp_start_state; a compound-wait request checks its condition exactly once on entering request-under-execution. No execution-delay timer exists and every ready ticket advances through all states in one Pump call. TC18 §12.9.3 Table 26 (TC18.txt:3289-3341).

requirements.title: Trigger observation and delay start are independent of endpoint idleness
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A dispatcher shall record trigger-condition fulfilment and start the request's trigger exec-delay timer at the moment the trigger is observed, regardless of whether the endpoint is executing another request. Trigger sources are polled only while iterating tickets already started. TC18 §12.9.3 (TC18.txt:3344-3346).

requirements.title: A full endpoint request storage drops the new request and answers REQ_storage_OVFL
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — request.Dispatcher shall enforce a configured maximum number of non-finalized tickets, reject a further Submit with a distinct sentinel, and udp.errorCodeFor shall render that sentinel as udp.ErrorCodeRequestStorageOverflow. Submit is unbounded today and that error code is produced by no path. TC18 §12.9.3 (TC18.txt:3347-3349) and §12.9.6 Table 27 (TC18.txt:3430).

requirements.title: A full responder queue evicts the lowest sequence_num and flags overflow
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When a responder queue is full and a further response is delivered, the server shall discard the queued AVTPDU with the lowest sequence_num, enqueue the new response, and set that queue's overflow bit. Neither the queue nor the overflow bit exists. TC18 §12.9.4 (TC18.txt:3378-3380).

requirements.title: A full acknowledge queue evicts the lowest sequence_num and flags overflow
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When an acknowledge queue is full and a further acknowledge is delivered, the server shall discard the queued AVTPDU with the lowest sequence_num, enqueue the new acknowledge, and set that queue's overflow bit. TC18 §12.9.5 (TC18.txt:3388-3390).

requirements.title: An endpoint execution failure is reported as EP_ERROR, not INVALID_PARAMETER
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — udp.errorCodeFor shall map an error originating from a request.Handler's execution — as distinct from request decoding or validation — to udp.ErrorCodeEPError, reserving udp.ErrorCodeInvalidParameter for out-of-range request parameters. A hardware or execution failure currently falls through to the malformed-parameter code, and ErrorCodeEPError is selected by no path. TC18 §12.9.6 (TC18.txt:3407-3408) and Table 27 (TC18.txt:3424).

requirements.title: Error responses are timestamped when the endpoint is configured for it
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When an endpoint's timestamp-error-responses configuration is set, the error response shall be acf.KindLong with MTV true and a populated Timestamp. The error-response builder copies the request's Kind and sets no timestamp. TC18 §12.9.6 (TC18.txt:3409).

requirements.title: udp.ErrorCode transcribes Table 27's seventeen-entry enumeration exactly
requirements.text: udp.ErrorCode shall define exactly the seventeen codes of TC18 Table 27 at their specified numeric values, from UNSUPPORTED_CMD = 1 through CHAIN_ERROR = 17, and ErrorCode.Valid shall accept exactly those values and reject 0 and any value of 18 or more. TC18 §12.9.6 Table 27 (TC18.txt:3414-3446).

requirements.title: An unknown sequencer is answered SEQUENCER_NOT_KNOWN
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A request naming a sequencer beyond the server's configured sequencer count shall be answered with udp.ErrorCodeSequencerNotKnown. request.Sequencer auto-creates every identifier on first use, so the condition never arises and the code is produced by no path. TC18 §12.9.6 Table 27 (TC18.txt:3416) and §12.10 (TC18.txt:3472-3473).

requirements.title: Sequencer identifiers and state values are bounded at 256
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The number of sequencers and the number of states per sequencer are limited to 256, and a server may support fewer; request.SequencerID is uint16 and the state register is uint32 with saturation, both wider than the specification allows, while GeneralBlock.NumSequencerStates has the correct width but is never set. A count of zero shall mean sequencer operation is unsupported. TC18 §12.10 (TC18.txt:3472-3473).

requirements.title: A not-used endpoint accepts no pin assignments and validates no requests
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap.PinMap.Validate shall reject an assignment referencing an endpoint whose ep_used bit is clear, and the dispatch path shall reject a request addressed to such an endpoint rather than executing it. The Enabled flag is carried but consulted only by the encoder. TC18 §13.1 (TC18.txt:3502-3503).

requirements.title: A granted non-root stream can write only an endpoint's functional block
requirements.text: For a non-root requester holding a grant for an endpoint, the server shall expose no path that mutates that endpoint's generic block (ep_type, ep_used, pin mapping) — only its functional block. TC18 §13.1 (TC18.txt:3516-3518).

requirements.title: The generic endpoint block carries Table 28's full twelve-octet layout
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap's generic endpoint block shall carry ep_type, ep_used, ep_delay_time, ep_req_storage_size, ep_description, ep_tx_buffer_size and ep_rx_buffer_size at TC18 Table 28's relative offsets and bit positions within a twelve-octet, 0x000C-stride block. The current block is a bespoke three-byte record of address, type and enabled. TC18 §13.2 Table 28 (TC18.txt:3541-3582).

requirements.title: EndpointType constants carry Table 29's own numeric values
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — regmap.EndpointType shall assign each endpoint kind exactly the value TC18 Table 29 gives it — Server 0x00, WakeUp Ctrl 0x01, GPIO 0x02, SPI 0x03, I2C 0x04, UART 0x05, LIN 0x06, PWM_OUT 0x07, PWM_IN 0x08, ADC 0x09, DAC 0x0A, CAN 0x0B, ISELED 0x0C, MDIO 0x0D — so a decoded ep_type byte names the endpoint kind a conformant peer meant. The current constants are a locally invented iota run in which every value disagrees. TC18 §13.2 Table 29 (TC18.txt:3601-3618).

requirements.title: EP0's ep_used bit is fixed at 1
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The generic endpoint block for regmap.EP0 shall always encode ep_used = 1, since EP0 must always be implemented, and a write attempting to clear it shall be rejected. TC18 §13.2 Table 28 (TC18.txt:3551-3553).

requirements.title: EP_RESP_ON_ERROR gauges driven pins and names the failing pin in the error response
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When an endpoint's EP_RESP_ON_ERROR option is set, every pin-driving endpoint shall read back each pin it drove and, for a pin whose state does not follow the commanded value, return an error response carrying that pin's reference; an error from a different source shall produce an error response with the corresponding error code. No EP_RESP_ON_ERROR field, pin read-back or pin-reference response field exists. TC18 §13.2 (TC18.txt:3585-3588).

requirements.title: A server without time synchronization can be configured to execute a timed request rather than drop it
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — avtp.Header.Disposition and its caller shall accept a policy selecting either DispositionDrop or DispositionBestEffort for a timed header on a server without time synchronization; TC18 names both alternatives and makes the choice a configuration matter, whereas Disposition hard-codes the drop. TC18 §13.3 (TC18.txt:3636-3638).

requirements.title: A tv=0 timestamped header is dispositioned as if untimed
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — avtp.Header.Disposition shall report DispositionBestEffort for a timed header whose timestamp is marked invalid (tv = 0) even when the caller reports no time-sync support, since such a request carries no presentation time and TC18 requires it to be queued as if the header were NTSCF; DispositionDrop is reserved for a header that genuinely carries a presentation time. Disposition tests time-sync support before looking at the timestamp status, so a tv=0 TSCF request is dropped today. TC18 §13.3 (TC18.txt:3639-3641).

requirements.title: An uncertain timestamp is scheduled exactly as a valid one
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — avtp.Header.Disposition shall report DispositionScheduled for a timed header whose timestamp is marked uncertain (tu = 1) on a time-sync-capable server, since TC18 requires tu = 1 to be executed as if tu = 0.
