The current code folds uncertain down to DispositionBestEffort, and REQ-AVTP-008 mandates that demotion. TC18 §13.3 (TC18.txt:3641-3642).

requirements.title: A compound-wait comparison caps a longer interface status and never matches a shorter one
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The §13.5.1 comparison shall report no match unconditionally when the endpoint's interface status is shorter than the byte_msg_payload, and shall truncate the interface status to the payload's length when it is longer — so a four-byte payload checks only the first four of twenty received SPI bytes. TC18 §13.5.1 (TC18.txt:3737-3740).

requirements.title: acf gains a compound-wait evt class implementing the eight §13.5.1 comparisons
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — acf shall provide a compound-wait classification of evt[2:0] distinct from ClassifyEVT's three Table 30 request-side rows, mapping 000b to exact match, 001b to payload-AND-status OR NOT-payload equal to all ones, 010b to payload-AND-status equal to zero, 100b/101b to first-half greater-or-equal / less-or-equal and 110b/111b to last-half greater-or-equal / less-or-equal over the first quadlet, and returning a reserved error for 011b that renders as udp.ErrorCodeUnsupportedCommand. Note 111b in this class is a comparison, not Table 30's configuration action, so reusing ClassifyEVT would be wrong. TC18 §13.5.1 (TC18.txt:3742-3764).

requirements.title: Safe-command mode is a discoverable, configurable bit of the endpoint register map
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The endpoint register map shall carry the plain/safe command-mode selection so a client can discover which endpoints are CRC-secured, and the server shall interpose e2e.Guard for exactly the endpoints whose bit is set. Protection is a construction-time wiring decision today, invisible on the wire. TC18 §13.6 (TC18.txt:3782-3787) and §13.7 Table 32 (TC18.txt:3913-3923).

requirements.title: e2e.Compute implements CRC32P4 with Table 31's exact parameters
requirements.text: e2e.Compute shall implement the CRC TC18 Table 31 specifies — polynomial 0xF4ACFB13, width 32, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF, input and output reflected — and not the IEEE 802.3 CRC-32, so a safe point this package produces is accepted by a conformant peer. TC18 §13.6 Table 31 (TC18.txt:3792-3807).

requirements.title: The safe point covers the AVTPDU header's avtp_timestamp, zeroed for NTSCF
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — e2e's CRC computation shall take the enclosing avtp.Header and include its avtp_timestamp field in the covered bytes, substituting all zeros when the header is NTSCF. The current computation takes only the StreamID and hashes the ACF message_timestamp, an entirely different field. TC18 §13.6 (TC18.txt:3809-3811).

requirements.title: The safe point covers the whole encoded ACF message header
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — e2e's CRC shall be computed over the ACF message's encoded wire bytes — acf_msg_type, acf_msg_length, pad, mtv, byte_bus_id, evt, rsv, hs, cs, transaction_num, the control bits and read_size/segment_num — rather than a bespoke subset of struct fields. evt, hs, cs, mtv, pad, acf_msg_type and acf_msg_length are uncovered today, so evt[2:0] can be altered in flight with the CRC still verifying. TC18 §13.6 (TC18.txt:3812) and Figures 19 and 20 (TC18.txt:3844-3881).

requirements.title: The covered header carries the CRC-inclusive lengths
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The acf_msg_length and the AVTPDU ntscf_data_length or stream_data_length values fed into the CRC shall already include the trailing CRC32 quadlet — plus one quadlet and plus four octets respectively. The encoders do produce the incremented wire lengths, but since those fields are not covered by the CRC the 'before CRC calculation' ordering cannot be implemented until the coverage span is corrected. TC18 §13.6 (TC18.txt:3813-3815).

requirements.title: Each ACF message in a multi-message AVTPDU carries and verifies its own safe point
requirements.text: For an AVTPDU carrying several ACF messages the CRC32 shall be computed per message, so each carries its own trailing safe point and a corrupt safe point on one message does not invalidate any other message in the same frame. TC18 §13.6 (TC18.txt:3789-3791).

requirements.title: Only the terminal segment of a fragmented sequence carries a safe point
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — fragment.Split shall place the trailing CRC32 and the corresponding length increases only on the segment with acf.FlagMoreSegments clear, and the reassembler shall reject a segment carrying FlagMoreSegments together with a trailing safe point. The combined-payload and terminal-segment verification half is covered by REQ-FRAG-009; rejecting a non-terminal segment that carries a CRC is not. TC18 §13.6 (TC18.txt:3816-3823).

requirements.title: A CRC mismatch skips execution and is reported as the Table 27 CRC error code
requirements.text: A request received in an end-to-end protected stream whose CRC does not match shall not be executed, and the error response shall carry udp.ErrorCodePOCIFailure, TC18 Table 27's code for a request CRC that does not match, rather than falling through to the generic invalid-parameter code. TC18 §13.6 (TC18.txt:3827-3828) and §12.9.6 Table 27 (TC18.txt:3432).

requirements.title: A protected body is payload, then pad, then the CRC32 quadlet
requirements.text: e2e.Protect shall assemble the protected body as the real payload, followed by zero to three zero pad bytes rounding the payload up to a whole quadlet, followed by the four-byte big-endian CRC32 as the final quadlet — never CRC before pad. TC18 §13.6 Figures 19 and 20 (TC18.txt:3843-3881).

requirements.title: Every endpoint's functional block reserves Table 32's common register header
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — Each endpoint type's EncodeConfig shall place ep_len at relative address 0x0000, ep_enable&clr at 0x0002 and ep_options at 0x0003, so a client patching ep_options at 0x0003 reaches that register on every endpoint type. Every endpoint package lays out its own fields from offset zero today, colliding with the reserved common pair. TC18 §13.7 Table 32 (TC18.txt:3900-3947).

requirements.title: A newly declared endpoint is enabled by default and EP0 is always enabled
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — Declaring an endpoint shall leave its ep_enable bit set, since TC18 makes 1b the power-on default, and a write clearing EP0's enable bit shall be rejected because EP0 is always enabled. regmap.GenericEndpointBlock.Enabled is a Go bool defaulting to false and is set by no constructor. TC18 §13.7 Table 32 (TC18.txt:3903-3907).

requirements.title: Writing ep_clear_req_storage purges the endpoint's request storage and reads back zero
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A write of 1b to relative address 0x0002 bit 4 of an endpoint's functional block shall discard every pending ticket that endpoint holds, and a subsequent read of that byte shall report bit 4 clear. No write-1-clears register exists. TC18 §13.7 Table 32 (TC18.txt:3909-3911).

requirements.title: Safe-mode CRC is selected per endpoint by ep_options bits 0 to 2
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — e2e.Guard shall consult the addressed endpoint's ep_options bits — 0x0003.0 request-CRC checking, .1 acknowledge-CRC generation, .2 response-CRC generation — verifying a request's trailing CRC32 only when bit 0 is set and appending a safe point to acknowledges and responses only when bits 1 and 2 respectively are set. Guard wraps a handler unconditionally at construction and has no separate acknowledge and response switches. TC18 §13.7 Table 32 (TC18.txt:3913-3923).

requirements.title: ep_error_stream routes error responses to the acknowledge stream
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The server shall place an error response on the addressed endpoint's acknowledge stream rather than its response stream when that endpoint's ep_options bit 0x0003.4 is set. There is one combined reply path today. TC18 §13.7 Table 32 (TC18.txt:3927-3931).

requirements.title: ep_options bits 6 and 7 suppress error and successful-write responses
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The server shall emit no reply for an error response when the addressed endpoint's ep_options bit 0x0003.6 is set, and none for a successful write request's response when bit 0x0003.7 is set, while still executing the request. No suppression configuration exists. TC18 §13.7 Table 32 (TC18.txt:3935-3944) and §12.9.1 (TC18.txt:3209-3212).

requirements.title: A configured response queue emits a heartbeat, falling back to a headers-only NTSCF PDU
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The server shall support sending a cyclic heartbeat by flushing a response queue on a fixed period, transmitting an AVTPDU carrying just an NTSCF header and no ACF types when the queue is empty. acf.EncodeFrame structurally accepts zero messages but no caller emits such a frame. TC18 §13.7.1.1 (TC18.txt:3967-3970).

requirements.title: EP0 register access uses the address-plus-data payload and Table 30's combining rules
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — An EP0 write's byte_msg_payload shall be decoded as a big-endian 16-bit register address followed by the data to write, and that data shall be combined into the addressed register under the request's evt[2:0] as SET, OR, AND or XOR. The EP0 path decodes the body as a whole encoded register map and never consults evt, so a client cannot OR, AND or XOR a server register. TC18 §13.7.1.1 (TC18.txt:3963-3966), §13.7.1.2 (TC18.txt:4000-4004, 4035-4044) and Figure 21 (TC18.txt:4011).

requirements.title: A write touching a read-only server register has no effect and is confirmed normally
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A write whose data would change a read-only register shall discard that portion and return an ordinary success response, since TC18 reserves an error response for write-prohibited registers only. WriteEP0 returns regmap.ErrGeneralBlockReadOnly instead, and REQ-RCS-011 pins that behaviour. TC18 §13.7.1.2 (TC18.txt:4039-4041).

requirements.title: A locked-register write is answered UNAUTHORIZED_ACCESS
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — udp.errorCodeFor shall map regmap.ErrRegisterLocked to udp.ErrorCodeUnauthorizedAccess, the code TC18 names for a write to a write-prohibited register such as the map-set lock bit; it currently maps to udp.ErrorCodeLockedMemAccess. TC18 §13.7.1.2 (TC18.txt:4040-4041).

requirements.title: svr_root_client_index is a register and a non-root EP0 write cannot reach other endpoints
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The RC Server register map shall expose svr_root_client_index as the request-stream index holding root write access, with zero meaning no stream has it, and a non-root stream's EP0 write shall be accepted when it touches only EP0's own registers while being rejected when it would change any other endpoint's block. Root ownership is modelled by an access controller keyed on StreamID with no register, and WriteEP0 is root-only outright. TC18 §13.7.1.2 Table 33 (TC18.txt:3985-3989, 4003-4005).

requirements.title: A PTP-capable server emits trigger references 0 and 1 on sync acquisition and loss
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A server reporting time-sync support shall queue a drainable trigger with reference number 0 when PTP time synchronization is established and reference number 1 when it is lost, so a client can gate timed requests on the server's clock validity. There is no server-side trigger queue and time-sync support is a static caller-supplied flag. TC18 §13.7.1.3 Table 34 (TC18.txt:4047-4054).

requirements.title: A wakeup-control endpoint may only be declared at byte_bus_id 1
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — Declaring an endpoint shall reject a wakeup-control endpoint at any address other than 1, and shall reject any other endpoint type at address 1, since TC18 fixes the WakeUp endpoint to endpoint number 1 as the only endpoint that stays active in sleep mode. Any address is accepted today. TC18 §13.7.2.1 (TC18.txt:4084-4086).

requirements.title: Wakeup configuration carries a null-terminated wake-source pin table
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — wakeup.Config shall carry a read-only wup_nr_io_pins_max and a table of 16-bit wake-source entries packing the IO pin number in bits [10:0] and the IO behaviour in bits [15:11], terminated by an entry whose pin number is zero. The config is three fields with no wake-source table at all. TC18 §13.7.2.2 Table 36 (TC18.txt:4100-4118).

requirements.title: A wake source's IO behaviour is one of Table 37's six defined encodings
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — wakeup shall define a wake-source behaviour type accepting exactly the six encodings of TC18 Table 37 — 00000b inactive, 00001b rising edge, 00010b falling edge, 00011b both edges, 00100b high level, 00101b low level — and rejecting every other five-bit value, which the table reserves. TC18 §13.7.2.2 Table 37 (TC18.txt:4136-4144).

requirements.title: wup_status reports which wake source fired and is cleared by writing one
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — wakeup.Endpoint shall maintain a 16-bit wup_status register in which each bit represents a wake-up source, setting the bit for the source that caused the most recent transition out of sleep and clearing each bit for which a client writes 1b. No such register exists, and TC18 §12.5 makes clearing it a precondition for re-entering sleep. TC18 §13.7.2.2 Table 36 (TC18.txt:4108-4110).

requirements.title: A debounce time suppresses wake-up on noise
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — wakeup.Config shall carry a debounce duration applied to every configured wake-source signal, and a source assertion shorter than that duration shall not cause a transition out of sleep. TC18 §13.7.2.2 (TC18.txt:4097).

requirements.title: A sleep request carries SleepCMD 0xA5
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — wakeup.EncodePowerStateRequest shall emit the byte 0xA5 for a request targeting sleep — the SleepCMD value TC18 Figure 22 fixes — and the decoder shall accept 0xA5 as sleep, rather than emitting this package's own enum ordinal 0x02. 0xA5 is a deliberate high-Hamming-distance sentinel on a safety-relevant command; the current bytes are frozen by a golden vector. TC18 §13.7.2.3 Figure 22 (TC18.txt:4160-4168).

requirements.title: Entering sleep is gated on every endpoint going idle and every responder queue draining
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — On a sleep request the server shall first stop admitting incoming requests to endpoint queues, then wait until every declared endpoint reports no pending timed or standard requests and every responder queue is empty, and only then acknowledge the request and enter sleep. The transition is applied immediately with no quiesce. TC18 §13.7.2.3 (TC18.txt:4149-4158).

requirements.title: SPI trigger events carry Table 38's reference numbers
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — spi.TriggerEvent shall expose a reference number of 0 for transfer-complete and 2 + 2*channel + (0 asserted, 1 de-asserted) for a chip-select edge, yielding 2 through 13 for CS0 through CS5, and shall never emit reference number 1, which Table 38 reserves. The event carries no reference number today and the internal chip-select-edge kind collides with the reserved slot. TC18 §13.7.3.1 Table 38 (TC18.txt:4205-4220).

requirements.title: SPI channel configuration carries every Table 39 per-channel parameter
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — spi.ChannelConfig shall carry spi_cs_polarity, spi_use_cs, spi_cs_clk_leadtime, spi_clk_cs_trailtime, spi_bits_max and spi_pause_min (in spi_clk cycles) at Table 39's relative offsets, and the configuration shall expose a read-only spi_nr_cs. Only clock, mode and an inter-transfer delay in microseconds exist today. TC18 §13.7.3.2 Table 39 (TC18.txt:4244-4296).

requirements.title: An SPI transfer appends zeros when read_size exceeds the payload length
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The SPI endpoint shall extend the transmitted byte sequence with zero bytes until it is at least read_size bytes long before handing it to the channel transport, so a read longer than the write still clocks the full requested count. read_size is never consulted by the SPI package. TC18 §13.7.3.3 (TC18.txt:4359) and Figure 23 (TC18.txt:4356).

requirements.title: An SPI transfer presents the full payload on PICO and truncates its response to read_size
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The SPI endpoint shall transmit the entire byte_msg_payload on PICO regardless of read_size, and shall truncate the response body to the first read_size received bytes when read_size is non-zero and smaller than the payload — Figure 23's twenty-byte write answered by a ten-byte response. The response currently returns the full received sequence. TC18 §13.7.3.3 (TC18.txt:4360-4361).

requirements.title: SPI retains the last received data, channel-independently, for wait comparison
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — spi.Endpoint shall retain the most recently received byte sequence from any channel up to read_size bytes, and a wait request shall compare its byte_msg_payload against that retained data irrespective of which chip-select channel produced it. The optional wait feature is not implemented and received bytes are discarded after each transfer. TC18 §13.7.3.1 (TC18.txt:4200-4202) and §13.7.3.3 (TC18.txt:4334-4336).

requirements.title: An SPI transfer halted on cs/hs latches an error state and disables the endpoint
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When a transfer stops on the request's cs or hs bits, spi.Endpoint shall record the condition in its status register, clear its enable bit, and reject every subsequent request until the client both clears the error status and re-enables the endpoint. The cs and hs bits are decoded but consulted nowhere in the SPI package and a transport error is not latched. TC18 §13.7.3.3 (TC18.txt:4337-4340).

requirements.title: A clamped SPI pin raises a server diagnostic flag and sets err on every response from that endpoint
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When an SPI endpoint detects a clamped (stuck at VDD or GND) pin it shall set the corresponding flag in the server's diagnostic registers and shall set acf.FlagError on every response it subsequently emits until the condition is cleared. No diagnostic register exists and the response builder never sets FlagError, so a stuck-pin fault currently produces indistinguishably successful responses. TC18 §13.7.3.3 (TC18.txt:4340-4342).

requirements.title: GPIO emits per-pin change, rising and falling triggers at Table 40's reference numbers
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — gpio.Endpoint shall queue a distinct trigger for each of change, rising edge and falling edge of every changed trigger-enabled pin, carrying reference numbers 3i+1, 3i+2 and 3i+3 for pin i, plus reference 0 on request-execution completion. One bitmask-valued event per write is queued today, so another endpoint cannot subscribe to a specific pin edge. TC18 §13.7.4.1 Table 40 (TC18.txt:4408-4420).

requirements.title: GPIO configuration carries Table 41's clock and per-pin debounce registers
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — gpio.Config shall carry gpio_io_max, gpio_base_clk (kHz, read-only), gpio_clk_divider and thirty-two per-pin gpio_debounce values at Table 41's relative offsets, where a debounce count n greater than zero requires n consecutive equal samples — taken at the divided base clock, independently of request arrival — before the pin's value changes. The config is pin count, direction and trigger-enable only. TC18 §13.7.4.2 Table 41 (TC18.txt:4439-4471) and §13.7.4.1 (TC18.txt:4385).

requirements.title: Each GPIO output pin carries a drive strength and an output topology
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — gpio.Config shall carry, for each pin its direction marks as an output, a configurable drive strength and an output topology selecting push-pull, open-drain or open-source, both ignored for input pins. Neither exists, and Table 41 allocates no offset for them — a spec-internal inconsistency worth raising upstream. TC18 §13.7.4.1 (TC18.txt:4386-4388).

requirements.title: A GPIO write, or a read carrying a payload, defers its response until debounce elapses
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — gpio.Endpoint shall answer a read request with an empty byte_msg_payload immediately, and shall, for a write request or a read carrying a payload, first apply the new drive and then defer the response until the configured debounce time has elapsed. Every path answers synchronously today and a read carrying a payload is not distinguished from a pure read. TC18 §13.7.4.3 (TC18.txt:4484-4486).

requirements.title: A GPIO wait request is evaluated against the live pin-value register
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — gpio.Endpoint shall evaluate a wait request's condition against its internal GPIO read register — the same word a read returns — rather than against sequencer state, gating the request's completion on that comparison. The endpoint handles only read and write and rejects everything else. TC18 §13.7.4.3 (TC18.txt:4478-4479).

requirements.title: An endpoint's trigger output can fire another endpoint's triggered request
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A dispatcher shall release a triggered request naming trigger reference number n when the endpoint owning reference n emits it, so that a GPIO endpoint's response can be generated by another endpoint's trigger. No endpoint's drained trigger events are registered as a dispatcher trigger source, and with no reference numbers there is no identifier for a triggered request to name. TC18 §13.7.4.1 (TC18.txt:4406) and §13.7.10.1 (TC18.txt:5279).

requirements.title: PWM_OUT emits Table 42's three numbered trigger signals
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — pwm.Endpoint shall emit three distinguishable trigger signals — index 0 on request-execution completion, index 1 at the start of each PWM cycle, index 2 at the midpoint of the active pulse, the last emitted even when the duty cycle is 0% — and pwm.TriggerEvent shall carry the Table 42 index. Only the execution-done trigger exists and events carry no index. TC18 §13.7.5.1 Table 42 (TC18.txt:4530-4537).

requirements.title: PWM_OUT functional configuration implements Table 43's register block
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — pwm's output configuration shall represent TC18 Table 43 at its relative addresses, including pwmo_base_clk (kHz, read-only), pwmo_clk_divider, pwmo_inv_polarity, pwmo_idle_state, pwmo_duty_cycle_min and _max, and pwmo_skew, with every read/write field writable at runtime. The current config is enable, role and two default tick counts. TC18 §13.7.5.2 Table 43 (TC18.txt:4562-4604).

requirements.title: PWM_OUT write requests are capped, not rejected, at the configured duty-cycle limits
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — pwm.Endpoint shall clamp a write request's active-time value up to pwmo_duty_cycle_min and down to pwmo_duty_cycle_max before applying it, reporting the clamped value rather than returning an error; TC18 says requests outside the limits are capped. Only an active-exceeds-period rejection exists. TC18 §13.7.5.2 Table 43 (TC18.txt:4589-4594).

requirements.title: A PWM_OUT request whose body is not exactly four bytes is rejected as INVALID_PARAMETER
requirements.text: A PWM_OUT request whose byte_msg_payload is not exactly four bytes shall be rejected, and the resulting decode error shall be rendered on the wire as udp.ErrorCodeInvalidParameter. TC18 §13.7.5.3 (TC18.txt:4630-4631) and §13.7.4.1 (TC18.txt:4391-4392) for GPIO.

requirements.title: A zero period stops PWM_OUT generation
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — pwm.Endpoint shall treat a PWM_OUT write whose period field is zero as a stop command, ceasing waveform generation and cycle-derived triggers and driving the output to its configured idle state, resuming on the next request with a non-zero period. Period zero is stored as an ordinary waveform today. TC18 §13.7.5.3 (TC18.txt:4641-4642).

requirements.title: A zero active time disables the PWM_OUT output while triggers continue
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A PWM_OUT write with active time zero and a non-zero period shall leave the endpoint running: the output is held inactive while the cycle-derived triggers continue at the configured period. TC18 §13.7.5.3 (TC18.txt:4643-4644).

requirements.title: A PWM_OUT trigger-configuration request's leading field is a phase shift
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When a PWM_OUT request is a trigger configuration, pwm shall decode the first two bytes of byte_msg_payload as a phase shift relative to the referenced source endpoint rather than as the period, and apply that offset to the generated waveform. Bytes 0-1 are decoded unconditionally as the period, so such a request is silently mis-applied. TC18 §13.7.5.3 (TC18.txt:4645-4646).

requirements.title: PWM_OUT monitors its own output pin for toggling and signals a stuck pin
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — pwm.Endpoint shall sample its own output pin while generating and shall signal an error when the pin does not toggle as commanded. pwm.OutputTransport is write-only with no read-back path. TC18 §13.7.5.3 (TC18.txt:4647-4648).

requirements.title: A complementary PWM_OUT pin is driven in opposite phase with the configured skew
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — If the optional inverted output is configured, pwm shall drive PWM_OUTN in opposite phase to PWM_OUT with the rising edges separated by pwmo_skew source-clock cycles for break-before-make behaviour, and shall derive the trigger signals from the delayed signal. The pin pair is named in the pin map but the transport drives a single waveform with no inversion or skew. TC18 §13.7.5.1 (TC18.txt:4515-4521).

requirements.title: PWM_IN functional configuration implements Table 45's register block
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — pwm's input configuration shall represent TC18 Table 45 at its relative addresses, including pwmi_base_clk, pwmi_clk_divider, pwmi_polarity, pwmi_err_on_max_period, pwmi_continuous_mode and pwmi_max_period, with bits 3 to 7 of offset 0x0009 reading zero. TC18 §13.7.6.2 Table 45 (TC18.txt:4696-4740).

requirements.title: PWM_IN detects an over-long period per pwmi_err_on_max_period and reports it only when enabled
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — pwm.Endpoint in input role shall detect an incoming period exceeding pwmi_max_period; with pwmi_err_on_max_period clear it shall invalidate the measurement and resynchronize on the next active phase, and with it set it shall stop measuring and return a signal-lost error only when the endpoint's EP_RESP_ON_ERR option is enabled. The error surface exists but there is no max-period register, no two-behaviour split and no response gate. TC18 §13.7.6.1 (TC18.txt:4668-4670) and §13.7.6.2 (TC18.txt:4721).

requirements.title: PWM_IN emits Table 44's rising- and falling-edge trigger signals
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — pwm.Endpoint in input role shall emit trigger index 0 on each rising edge and index 1 on each falling edge of the observed signal, with polarity taken from pwmi_polarity. The package offers a per-measurement trigger and a signal-lost trigger, neither of which is an edge. TC18 §13.7.6.1 Table 44 (TC18.txt:4671-4676).

requirements.title: pwmi_continuous_mode selects one-shot deferred versus continuous immediate responses
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — An input-role read shall, with pwmi_continuous_mode clear, start one measurement and defer the response until it finalizes, and with it set shall respond immediately with the most recent measurement. Only the immediate path exists and there is no register to select the other. TC18 §13.7.6.2 Table 45 (TC18.txt:4725-4731).

requirements.title: The I2C endpoint accepts a transfer request in either ACF_ABB or ACF_GBB
requirements.text: i2c.Endpoint shall accept a transfer request framed as either acf.KindShort (ACF_ABB) or acf.KindLong (ACF_GBB) and shall answer with a response of the same message kind. TC18 §13.7.7.1 (TC18.txt:4789-4791).

requirements.title: An I2C wait request resolves on a matching received bit sequence
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — If i2c.Endpoint supports TC18's optional wait request, it shall hold the request pending until the bytes received from the connected device match the request's expected sequence, then respond. The endpoint scopes to the plain request shape only. TC18 §13.7.7.1 (TC18.txt:4792-4793).

requirements.title: I2C functional configuration implements Table 46's register block
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — i2c.Config shall represent TC18 Table 46, including i2c_base_clk (read-only), i2c_clock_divider, i2c_mode and i2c_trail, with every read/write field changeable at runtime. The current config is enable, speed and a trailing time in microseconds. Note Table 46 assigns i2c_base_clk to 0x0002, colliding with i2c_ep_enable&clr — a spec defect whose adopted resolution must be recorded. TC18 §13.7.7.2 Table 46 (TC18.txt:4798-4826).

requirements.title: I2C enforces i2c_trail between consecutive transactions in I2C clock cycles
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — i2c.Endpoint shall not begin a transaction until at least i2c_trail I2C clock cycles, derived from the base clock and divider, have elapsed since the previous transaction completed. The configured trailing time is stored and round-tripped but read by no code, and its unit is microseconds rather than clock cycles. TC18 §13.7.7.2 Table 46 (TC18.txt:4821-4823).

requirements.title: The I2C endpoint is transparent to the address format
requirements.text: i2c.Endpoint shall place the request's byte_msg_payload on the bus verbatim including its leading address bytes, and shall never parse, validate or rewrite them, so 7-bit and 10-bit addressing are handled identically. TC18 §13.7.7.3 (TC18.txt:4830-4832) and Figure 29.

requirements.title: The I2C trigger signal's Table 47 index is unassigned in this specification revision
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — i2c.Endpoint emits one trigger per completed transfer, but TC18 Table 47 declares three I2C trigger signal indices with no event assigned to any of them, so the index that trigger should carry cannot be determined from the specification. No index shall be guessed; the ambiguity is recorded here and should be raised with the working group. TC18 §13.7.7.4 Table 47 (TC18.txt:4851-4857).

requirements.title: The UART receive FIFO is bounded by uart_rx_fifo_size and flags overflow
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — uart.Endpoint shall buffer at most uart_rx_fifo_size received bytes, discarding bytes that do not fit and setting the overflow flag in the UART status register, which is reported to the client and cleared through that register. The FIFO is an unbounded append today, which is also an unbounded-growth exposure when a peer never reads. TC18 §13.7.8.1 (TC18.txt:4881-4882).

requirements.title: A UART read completes on read_size, on uart_timeout, or on a full FIFO with a fragmented response
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — uart.Endpoint shall hold a read request until read_size bytes are available, until uart_timeout bit-times have elapsed, or — when the requested size exceeds uart_rx_fifo_size — until the FIFO is full, in which case the response shall be delivered as a fragmented sequence. The read path returns whatever is present immediately; the configured read timeout is read by no code. TC18 §13.7.8.1 (TC18.txt:4884-4889).

requirements.title: UART functional configuration implements Table 48's register block and its units
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — uart.Config shall represent TC18 Table 48, expressing baud rate in kbit/s as a 16-bit value, stop bits as a count of half stop bits, uart_timeout and uart_trail in bit times, and carrying uart_parity_enable and uart_parity_pol, uart_rts_enable and uart_cts_enable as separate fields, plus uart_half_duplex. The current config uses bit/s, a stop-bit enum, a single flow-control flag, a microsecond timeout, and adds mark/space parity the table cannot express. Note Table 48 names its enable and options rows after the PWM_IN registers and omits uart_rx_fifo_size entirely — spec defects worth raising upstream. TC18 §13.7.8.2 Table 48 (TC18.txt:4912-4961).

requirements.title: uart_half_duplex serializes transmit and receive
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When uart_half_duplex is set, uart.Endpoint shall not transmit while a reception is in progress and shall not accept received bytes while transmitting; with it clear transmit and receive proceed independently. Transmit and receive are wholly independent today, which is exactly what half-duplex forbids. TC18 §13.7.8.2 Table 48 (TC18.txt:4948-4950).

requirements.title: A payload-bearing UART read is rejected as an unknown command on the wire
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — udp.errorCodeFor shall render uart's payload-bearing-read rejection as udp.ErrorCodeUnsupportedCommand — TC18's UNKNOWN_CMD for this case — rather than letting it fall through to the generic invalid-parameter code. The Go-level rejection is correct and tested; only the wire code is wrong. TC18 §13.7.8.1 (TC18.txt:4890).

requirements.title: A UART compound-wait request resolves on a receive-FIFO content match
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — uart.Endpoint shall hold a compound-wait request pending until the receive FIFO's contents match the request's expected data, and shall reject an expected-data pattern longer than uart_rx_fifo_size as unsatisfiable. TC18 §13.7.8.1 (TC18.txt:4892-4894).

requirements.title: UART packs and unpacks sub-octet frames per uart_nr_bits
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When uart_nr_bits is not a multiple of eight, uart.Endpoint shall unpack the request payload into uart_nr_bits-wide symbols and discard the trailing padding bits, and shall pad each response payload to an integer number of octets. The payload is passed through byte-for-byte, so a configuration of 5, 6, 7 or 9 data bits — all of which the config accepts — silently mis-frames the wire. TC18 §13.7.8.3 (TC18.txt:4989-4993).

requirements.title: UART trigger index 1 fires on read-request completion
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — uart.Endpoint shall queue trigger index 1 when a read request is finalized — its byte count satisfied, its timeout expired, or its fragmented delivery complete — distinct from any internal receive-data-arrival notification. Index 1 currently fires on data arrival and the read path queues no trigger at all, so a consumer chaining off Table 49's index 1 fires on the wrong event and never on the right one. TC18 §13.7.8.4 Table 49 (TC18.txt:4999-5006).

requirements.title: ADC emits Table 50's four threshold-crossing triggers plus the interval trigger
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — adc.Endpoint shall compare each averaged value against adc_trigger_min and adc_trigger_max and emit trigger index 0 or 1 on a falling or rising crossing of the minimum, index 2 or 3 on a falling or rising crossing of the maximum, and index 4 on completion of each measurement interval, carrying the Table 50 index on each event. Only the measurement-done trigger exists, and threshold triggering is the mechanism by which an ADC drives other endpoints. TC18 §13.7.9.1 Table 50 (TC18.txt:5050-5058).

requirements.title: An ADC response carries read_size divided by two measurement values
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — adc.Endpoint shall return read_size / 2 consecutive 16-bit measurement values in the response body, each spaced by adc_sample_interval, rather than a single value. read_size is never consulted, so a Figure 33 request asking for eight measurements receives one. TC18 §13.7.9.3 (TC18.txt:5162-5163) and Figures 33 and 34 (TC18.txt:5177-5212).

requirements.title: A plain ADC request is payload-less and a wait request is not
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — adc.Endpoint shall reject a plain ADC request carrying a non-empty byte_msg_payload and shall reject a compound-wait ADC request that carries none. Body length is never inspected, and the evt path does not catch it because the config-only evt class permits evt=000b with a payload. TC18 §13.7.9.3 (TC18.txt:5162).

requirements.title: ADC functional configuration implements Table 51 and its sample, average and combine model
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — adc.Config shall represent TC18 Table 51, including adc_base_clk and adc_base_clk_divider, adc_sample_interval, adc_avg_intervals_per_request, adc_samples_per_avg_interval, adc_combine_avg_values as the count of averaging results per response frame, adc_resolution, and adc_trigger_min and adc_trigger_max, with samples within one request spaced by adc_sample_interval ticks. Only resolution and a sample count map across, and adc.CombineMode is a false friend: it is a smoothing rule between successive values, not TC18's count of averaging results packed into one response. TC18 §13.7.9.2 Table 51 (TC18.txt:5081-5126) and §13.7.9.1 (TC18.txt:5037-5042).

requirements.title: A combined ADC response carries the transaction_num of the request that produced its first average
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When adc_combine_avg_values exceeds adc_avg_intervals_per_request, adc.Endpoint shall accumulate averages across successive request executions and emit one response whose TransactionNum is that of the request generating the first average included, and shall emit multiple responses per execution when the combine count is the smaller value. The response always copies the current request's transaction number and exactly one response is emitted per request. TC18 §13.7.9.2 (TC18.txt:5128-5133).

requirements.title: An ADC response timestamp marks the last sample of its first average
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — When an ADC response carries a timestamp it shall be the capture time of the last raw sample contributing to the first average value included in the response, not the response-construction time. The response builder never sets Timestamp, so an ACF_GBB ADC response goes out with a zero timestamp. TC18 §13.7.9.2 (TC18.txt:5144-5145).

requirements.title: An ADC compound-wait request never samples
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — adc.Endpoint shall answer a compound-wait request by comparing its expected value against the last acquired average only, and shall never invoke the sampling path or the configured transport while doing so, regardless of trigger mode. The read path does sample in on-demand mode, so a wait routed through it would violate the clause directly. TC18 §13.7.9.1 (TC18.txt:5063).

requirements.title: Self-triggering generates ADC responses cyclically at a configured cycle time
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — An adc.Endpoint configured for self-triggering shall generate responses cyclically at its configured cycle time by chaining each measurement-completion trigger into the next measurement, rather than requiring an external caller to invoke the sampling entry point. The self-trigger mode is metadata only and there is no cycle-time configuration. TC18 §13.7.9.1 (TC18.txt:5033-5034).

requirements.title: A LIN read request arms a pending payload match that replies when a message matches
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — lin.Endpoint shall accept a read request by arming a pending match against the request's byte_msg_payload, compare every subsequently received message against it under the evt[2:0]-selected match condition, and emit the reply only when op = 0. The endpoint rejects any request without the write flag and has no read path, pending-match registry or received-message comparison at all. TC18 §13.7.10.1 (TC18.txt:5275-5277).

requirements.title: LIN's evt[2:0] match-condition reading is reconciled against Table 30's config-only row
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The reading of evt[2:0] for LIN shall be reconciled with TC18 §13.7.10.1's statement that evt[2:0] gives the match condition for a pending LIN read: either a LIN-specific evt class decoding match conditions is added, or the departure is documented the same way the existing Table 30 departures are. Table 30 places LIN in the config-only row, so REQ-LINEP-009 and REQ-EVT-003 reject evt[2:0] values 001b-110b, which makes every conditioned LIN read structurally unreachable. TC18 §13.7.10.1 (TC18.txt:5276-5277) versus §13.5 Table 30.

requirements.title: A LIN transaction trigger is queued only after the configured trailing time has elapsed
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — lin.Endpoint shall queue its transaction-complete trigger only once the transfer has finalized and the configured trailing time has elapsed, so a completed transfer whose trailing time is still running reports no event. The trigger is appended immediately after the transfer returns, and the trailing-time field is read by no code anywhere in the repository. TC18 §13.7.10.1 (TC18.txt:5278-5279).

requirements.title: LIN functional configuration implements Table 52's register block
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — lin's configuration codec shall lay out lin_ep_len, lin_ep_enable&clr, lin_ep_options, lin_base_clk, lin_ep_status and lin_clk_divider at their specified offsets and widths, with bit time derived from the base clock and divider, and every read/write field writable at runtime. The current seven-byte block carries none of those names and expresses baud rate directly. TC18 §13.7.10.2 Table 52 (TC18.txt:5284-5300).

requirements.title: can.Format encodes Table 54's six FrameFormat values
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — can's frame encoder shall emit the FrameFormat field as CBFF = 0, CEFF = 1, FBFF = 2, FEFF = 3, XL on the classic physical layer = 4 and XL on the new physical layer = 5, folding the standard/extended identifier distinction into that single field, and shall reject the reserved values 6 and 7. The package defines three format values and carries standard-versus-extended in a separate flags byte, so a classical extended frame encodes as format 0 with a flag where TC18 requires 1. TC18 §13.7.11.3 Table 54 (TC18.txt:5447-5456) and Figure 39 (TC18.txt:5428-5440).

requirements.title: CAN XL physical-layer selection is configurable and reaches the FrameFormat field
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — can.Config shall carry the CAN XL new-physical-layer selection and the encoder shall emit FrameFormat 4 for an XL frame on the classic physical layer and 5 on the new one. Neither the config nor the frame type has any physical-layer selector. TC18 §13.7.11.2 (TC18.txt:5356) and Table 54 (TC18.txt:5447-5456).

requirements.title: An 11-bit CAN identifier is right-aligned in the wire CAN ID field
requirements.text: can's frame encoder shall place a standard (non-extended) identifier right-aligned in the CAN ID field, so the encoded field's value equals the identifier with the upper bits zero. TC18 §13.7.11.3 (TC18.txt:5471).

requirements.title: A CAN endpoint cannot transmit a remote frame
requirements.text: can.Frame shall carry no remote-transmission-request field and can.Endpoint shall provide no path to transmit a remote frame; every transmitted frame is a data frame. TC18 §13.7.11.3 (TC18.txt:5471).

requirements.title: A CAN XL frame exceeding one ACF message is carried via ms and segment_num segmentation
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — A CAN XL frame whose encoded length — up to 2054 bytes, 2048 data plus the six XL header bytes — exceeds one ACF message shall be carried as a fragment sequence using the more-segments flag and the segment number, and the endpoint shall accept the reassembled body. The generic fragment machinery exists but the CAN endpoint decodes exactly one whole frame from the request body and never consults the segmentation fields. TC18 §13.7.11.3 (TC18.txt:5443-5444).

requirements.title: A CAN XL frame's six extra header bytes are the leading bytes of the CAN data field
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — For FrameFormat 4 or 5 the encoder shall emit the RRS, SDT, VCID and AF bytes — six in total per ISO 11898-1 — as the leading bytes of the CAN data field itself, so the field length is six plus the data length, rather than as a distinct region preceding a separate length prefix. The package encodes SDT, VCID and AF as a separate header and does not model RRS; its own documentation flags the layout as unverified. TC18 §13.7.11.3 (TC18.txt:5472-5473).

requirements.title: CAN functional configuration implements Table 53's register block
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — can's configuration codec shall lay out can_ep_len, a reserved byte reading zero, can_ep_enable&clr, can_ep_options, can_base_clk, can_ep_status, can_clk_divider, the three 32-bit bit-time registers for Classical, FD and XL, TDCC, the CAN EP and FIFO status words, four XL acceptance filters and four receive identifier filters at their specified offsets, accepting runtime writes to every read/write field. The current nine-byte block has no endpoint clock — which TC18 makes the time base for triggered and compound execution delays — and only two bit rates where the specification names three. Table 53 assigns both acceptance filter 3 and filter 4 to 0x002C, an editorial defect whose adopted resolution must be recorded. TC18 §13.7.11.2 Table 53 (TC18.txt:5363-5423) and (TC18.txt:5351-5360).

requirements.title: A CAN read request can wait for a specific received payload
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — can.Endpoint shall support a read request that waits for a frame matching the request's supplied payload or identifier criteria, producing its response upon that frame's reception, rather than only returning the last frame recorded. TC18 §13.7.11.1 (TC18.txt:5343-5346).

requirements.title: The ISELED endpoint performs 4b/5b encoding on transmit and 5b/4b decoding on receive
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — iseled.Endpoint shall 4b/5b-encode the command bytes it places on the chain and 5b/4b-decode the responses it collects, so a transport sees line-coded symbols and the aggregated response carries decoded payload bytes. No such codec exists; the package documentation declares 4b/5b a physical-layer concern outside its scope, whereas TC18 places the coding inside the endpoint. TC18 §13.7.12.1 (TC18.txt:5492-5494).

requirements.title: An ISELED aggregated response respects read_size and spans multiple ACF messages when needed
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — iseled.Endpoint shall bound the aggregated response by the request's read_size and emit the remainder as further ACF messages rather than one unbounded body. read_size is never consulted. TC18 §13.7.12.1 (TC18.txt:5493-5494).

requirements.title: ISELED CRC generation is configurable and the CRC field is four bits wide
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — iseled.Config shall carry a CRC-enable selection, the encoder shall append the CRC only when enabled and the decoders shall verify it only when enabled, and the CRC field shall be four bits wide. The package always appends and always requires an eight-bit CRC with no enable flag. TC18 §13.7.12.1 (TC18.txt:5494-5496) and §13.7.12.3 Figure 41 (TC18.txt:5600).

requirements.title: ISELED request and response bodies follow Figures 40 and 41
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — iseled.Command shall carry a 4-bit Instruction and a 12-bit Address emitted packed in that order ahead of the data bytes, and the aggregated response shall emit each device's answer as 12-bit address, 12-bit data, optional 4-bit CRC and reserved, without a leading count byte. The current encoding is an 8-bit address, a 16-bit data length, the data and an 8-bit CRC, with no instruction field at all. TC18 §13.7.12.3 Figures 40 and 41 (TC18.txt:5581-5610).

requirements.title: ISELED functional configuration implements Table 55, including a 16-bit LED count
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — iseled.Config shall carry iseled_base_clk, iseled_ep_status, iseled_clk_divider (nominally 2 MHz), the iseled_collect_resp and iseled_use_rcv_clk bits, a 16-bit iseled_nr_leds device count and a 16-bit iseled_rcv_timeout in ISELED clock tics, at Table 55's offsets, and the broadcast device address shall lie outside the widened device-index range. The current six-byte block uses an 8-bit device count — so chains above 255 LEDs are unrepresentable and the 0xFF broadcast sentinel collides with a real index once widened — and a 32-bit microsecond timeout. TC18 §13.7.12.2 Table 55 (TC18.txt:5504-5547).

requirements.title: ISELED receive clocking selects Freq_Sync or the ISP_N clock, and ISP_N may be left unmapped
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The iseled_use_rcv_clk bit shall select between Freq_Sync-pattern clock recovery and data sampling from the clock provided on ISP_N, and the pin map shall accept an ISELED endpoint that assigns ISP_P without assigning ISP_N when Freq_Sync is selected. Nothing in the repository models the selection. TC18 §13.7.12.2 (TC18.txt:5549-5551).

requirements.title: mdio.Mode's wire values are Table 57's mdio_mode encodings
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The MDIO encoders shall emit mdio_mode as 00b for MMD single-word, 01b for MMD multiple-byte, 10b for MMS single-word and 11b for MMS multiple-double-word access, and the adopted resolution of Table 57's duplicated 01b row shall be documented. The package assigns the four modes by iota and no requirement pins the numeric values against the table, so the ambiguity is currently undocumented. TC18 §13.7.13.3 Table 57 (TC18.txt:5676-5684).

requirements.title: mdio_address is wide enough for the IEEE and OPEN Alliance SPI register address space
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The MDIO request's address field shall be wide enough to carry the IEEE 802.3 / OPEN Alliance SPI register address for the selected mode — sixteen bits for an MMS access — and the encoders shall place it in Figure 42's mdio_address field rather than truncating it to six bits, with validation currently narrowing it further to five. TC18 §13.7.13.3 Figure 42 (TC18.txt:5664-5673) and Table 57 (TC18.txt:5681).

requirements.title: MDIO multiple-access modes carry more than one data unit
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — The MDIO write-request and response codecs shall carry a caller-supplied count of data units for the MMD multiple-byte and MMS multiple-double-word modes and recover all of them, rather than restricting those modes to a single data unit. Today the multiple modes are byte-for-byte identical to the single ones apart from the two mode bits. TC18 §13.7.13.3 Table 57 (TC18.txt:5677-5680).

requirements.title: MDIO payload width follows Table 57's MMD, MMS0-1 and other-MMS rule
requirements.text: The MDIO request's data width shall be two bytes for either MMD mode, four bytes for an MMS mode whose selected MMS index is 0 or 1, and two bytes for every other MMS index, and the encoders shall emit exactly that many payload bytes. TC18 §13.7.13.3 Table 57 (TC18.txt:5682-5683).

requirements.title: MDIO functional configuration implements Table 56's four register entries
requirements.text: NOT IMPLEMENTED — mdio's configuration codec shall lay out mdio_ep_len at 0x0000, a reserved byte reading zero at 0x0001, mdio_ep_enable&clr at 0x0002 and mdio_ep_options at 0x0003, carrying no further configurable parameters since TC18 states the MDIO endpoint has none. The current config is a single enable byte. Table 56 assigns mdio_ep_status to 0x0002, colliding with mdio_ep_enable&clr — an editorial defect whose adopted resolution must be recorded. TC18 §13.7.13.2 Table 56 (TC18.txt:5636-5657).
